1.1: These are the words which Mosheh spoke to all Yisra’ĕl beyond the Yardĕn in the wilderness, in the desert plain opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, and Laḇan, and Ḥatsĕroth, and Di Zahaḇ,
1.2: eleven days from Ḥorĕḇ by way of Mount Sĕ’ir to Qaḏĕsh Barnĕa.
1.3: And it came to be in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first of the month, that Mosheh spoke to the children of Yisra’ĕl according to all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded him concerning them,
1.4: after he had smitten Siḥon meleḵ of the Amorites, who dwelt in Ḥeshbon, and Oḡ meleḵ of Bashan, who dwelt at Ashtaroth in Eḏre’i.
1.5: Beyond the Yardĕn, in the land of Mo’aḇ, Mosheh undertook to declare this Torah, saying,
1.6: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim spoke to us in Ḥorĕḇ, saying, ‘You have dwelt long enough at this mountain.
1.7: ‘Turn and depart on your way, and go into the mountains of the Amorites, and to all the neighboring places in the desert plain, in the mountains and in the low country, and in the Negeḇ and on the seacoast, to the land of the Kena’anites and to Leḇanon, as far as the great river, the River Perath.
1.8: ‘See, I have put the land before you. Go in and possess the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 swore to your fathers, to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya’aqoḇ, to give to them and their seed after them.’
1.9: “And I spoke to you at that time, saying, ‘I am unable to bear you by myself.
1.10: ‘E𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has increased you, and see, you are today as numerous as the stars of the shamayim.
1.11: ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of your fathers is going to add to you a thousand times more than you are, and baraḵ you as He has spoken to you!
1.12: ‘How do I bear your pressure and your burden and your strife, by myself?
1.13: ‘Choose men, wise and understanding, and known to your tribes, and let me appoint them as your heads.’
1.14: “And you answered me and said, ‘The word which you have spoken to us to do is good.’
1.15: “And I took the heads of your tribes, wise men and known, and made them heads over you, leaders of thousands, and leaders of hundreds, and leaders of fifties, and leaders of tens, and officers for your tribes.
1.16: “And I commanded your judges at that time, saying, ‘When hearing between your brothers, judge righteously between a man and his brother or the stranger who is with him.
1.17: ‘Do not show partiality in right-ruling, hear the small as well as the great. Do not be afraid of anyone’s face, for the right-ruling belongs to Elohim. And the case which is too hard for you, bring it to me, and I shall hear it.’
1.18: “And I commanded you at that time all the words which you should do.
1.19: “Then we departed from Ḥorĕḇ, and went through all that great and awesome wilderness which you saw on the way to the mountains of the Amorites, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim had commanded us. And we came to Qaḏĕsh Barnĕa.
1.20: “And I said to you, ‘You have come to the mountains of the Amorites, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim is giving us.
1.21: ‘See, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has put the land before you. Go up and possess it, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of your fathers has spoken to you. Do not fear, nor be discouraged.’
1.22: “And all of you came near to me and said, ‘Let us send men before us, and let them search out the land for us, and bring back word to us of the way by which we should go up, and of the cities into which we would come.’
1.23: “And the matter was good in my eyes, so I took twelve of your men, one man from each tribe.
1.24: “And they turned and went up into the mountains, and came to the wadi Eshkol, and spied it out.
1.25: “And they took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us. And they brought back word to us, saying, ‘The land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim is giving us is good.’
1.26: “But you would not go up and rebelled against the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim,
1.27: and grumbled in your tents, and said, ‘Because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was hating us, He has brought us out of the land of Mitsrayim to give us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us.
1.28: ‘Where are we going to? Our brothers have made our hearts melt, saying, “The people are greater and taller than we, the cities are great and walled up to the shamayim, and we saw the sons of the Anaqim there too.” ’
1.29: “Then I said to you, ‘Have no dread or fear of them.
1.30: ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, who is going before you, He fights for you, according to all He did for you in Mitsrayim before your eyes,
1.31: and in the wilderness, where you saw how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has borne you, as a man bears his son, in all the way that you went until you came to this place.’
1.32: “Yet in this matter you are putting no trust in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim,
1.33: who is going before you in the way to seek out a place for you to pitch your tents, to show you the way you should go, in fire by night and in a cloud by day.
1.34: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 heard the voice of your words, and was wroth, and took an oath, saying,
1.35: ‘Not one of these men of this evil generation shall see that good land of which I swore to give to your fathers,
1.36: except Kalĕḇ son of Yephunneh. He shall see it, and to him and his children I give the land on which he walked, because he followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 completely.’
1.37: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was enraged with me for your sakes, saying, ‘You do not go in there, either.
1.38: ‘Yahoshua the son of Nun, who stands before you, he shall go in there. Strengthen him, for he shall cause Yisra’ĕl to inherit.
1.39: ‘And your little ones and your children, who you say are for a prey, who today have no knowledge of good and evil, they are going in there. And to them I give it, and they are to possess it.
1.40: ‘But you, turn and take your journey into the wilderness by the Way of the Sea of Reeds.’
1.41: “Then you answered and said to me, ‘We have sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. We ourselves are going up, and we shall fight, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim commanded us.’ And when each one of you had girded on his battle gear, you were ready to go up into the mountain.
1.42: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, ‘Say to them, “Do not go up nor fight, for I am not in your midst, lest you be smitten before your enemies.” ’
1.43: “So I spoke to you, but you would not listen and rebelled against the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and acted proudly, and went up into the mountain.
1.44: “Then the Amorites who dwelt in that mountain came out against you and chased you as bees do, and beat you back from Sĕ’ir to Ḥormah.
1.45: “And you returned and wept before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 would not listen to your voice nor give ear to you.
1.46: “So you dwelt in Qaḏĕsh many days, according to the days that you dwelt.

10.1: “At that time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, ‘Hew for yourself two tablets of stone like the first, and come up to Me on the mountain. And you shall make yourself an ark of wood,
10.2: then I write on the tablets the Words that were on the first tablets, which you broke. And you shall put them in the ark.’
10.3: “So I made an ark of acacia wood, hewed two tablets of stone like the first, and went up the mountain, with the two tablets in my hand.
10.4: “And He wrote on the tablets according to the first writing, the Ten Words, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had spoken to you in the mountain from the midst of the fire in the day of the assembly. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 gave them to me,
10.5: and I turned and came down from the mountain, and put the tablets in the ark which I had made. And they are there, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded me.”
10.6: Now the children of Yisra’ĕl departed from the wells of Benĕy Ya’aqan to Mosĕrah. Aharon died there, and he was buried there. And El’azar his son became kohĕn in his place.
10.7: From there they departed to Guḏgoḏah, and from Guḏgoḏah to Yotḇathah, a land of rivers of water.
10.8: At that time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 separated the tribe of Lĕwi to bear the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to stand before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to serve Him, and to baraḵ in His Name, to this day.
10.9: Therefore Lĕwi has no portion nor inheritance with his brothers. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is his inheritance, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim promised him.
10.10: “And I stayed in the mountain for forty days and forty nights. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 heard me at that time also, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 chose not to destroy you.
10.11: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, ‘Arise, go before the people, to depart, and let them go in and possess the land which I swore to their fathers to give them.’
10.12: “And now, Yisra’ĕl, what is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim asking of you, but to revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, to walk in all His Ways and to love Him, and to serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim with all your heart and with all your being,
10.13: to guard the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and His Laws which I command you today for your good?
10.14: “See, the shamayim and the shamayim of shamayim belong to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, also the earth with all that is in it.
10.15: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 delighted only in your fathers, to love them. And He chose their seed after them, you above all peoples, as it is today.
10.16: “And you shall circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and harden your neck no more.
10.17: “For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is Elohim of mighty ones and Aḏon of masters, the great Ĕl, mighty and awesome, who shows no partiality nor takes a bribe.
10.18: “He executes right-ruling for the fatherless and the widow, and loves the stranger, giving him food and a garment.
10.19: “And you shall love the stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Mitsrayim.
10.20: “Revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim. Serve Him, and cling to Him, and swear by His Name.
10.21: “He is your praise, and He is your Elohim, who has done for you these great and awesome deeds which your eyes have seen.
10.22: “Your fathers went down to Mitsrayim with seventy beings, and now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has made you as numerous as the stars of the shamayim.

11.1: “And you shall love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim and guard His Charge: even His Laws, and His Right-Rulings, and His Commands, always.
11.2: “And you shall know today - for it is not your children who have not known and who have not seen the discipline of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, His greatness, His strong hand and His outstretched arm,
11.3: and His signs, and His works which He had done in the midst of Mitsrayim, to Pharaoh meleḵ of Mitsrayim, and to all his land;
11.4: and that which He had done to the army of Mitsrayim, to their horses and their chariots, when He made the waters of the Sea of Reeds overflow them as they pursued you, and how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has destroyed them to this day;
11.5: and what He had done for you in the wilderness till you came to this place;
11.6: and what He had done to Dathan and Aḇiram the sons of Eliyaḇ, son of Re’uḇĕn, when the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up, and their households, and their tents, and all the living creatures that were in their possession, in the midst of all Yisra’ĕl.
11.7: “For yours are the eyes that saw all the great work of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, which He did.
11.8: “And you shall guard every Command which I command you today, so that you are strong, and shall go in, and shall possess the land which you are passing over to possess,
11.9: and to prolong your days in the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 swore to give your fathers, to them and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
11.10: “For the land which you are going in to possess is not like the land of Mitsrayim from which you have come, where you sowed your seed and watered it by foot, as a vegetable garden,
11.11: but the land which you are passing over to possess is a land of hills and valleys, which drinks water from the rain of the shamayim,
11.12: a land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim looks after. The eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim are always on it, from the beginning of the year to the latter end of the year.
11.13: ‘And it shall be that if you diligently obey My Commands which I command you today, to love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your being,
11.14: then I shall give you the rain for your land in its season, the early rain and the latter rain, and you shall gather in your grain, and your new wine, and your oil.
11.15: ‘And I shall give grass in your fields for your livestock, and you shall eat and be satisfied.
11.16: ‘Guard yourselves, lest your heart be deceived, and you turn aside and serve other mighty ones and bow down to them.
11.17: ‘Then the displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall burn against you, and He shall shut up the shamayim, and there be no rain, and the land not give its increase. And you shall perish quickly from the good land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is giving you.
11.18: ‘And you shall lay up these Words of Mine in your heart and in your being, and shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes.
11.19: ‘And you shall teach them to your children, speaking of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up,
11.20: and shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
11.21: so that your days and the days of your children are increased on the land of which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 swore to your fathers to give them, as the days of the shamayim on the earth.
11.22: ‘For if you diligently guard all these Commands which I command you, to do it, to love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, to walk in all His Ways, and to cling to Him,
11.23: then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall drive out all these nations before you, and you shall dispossess greater and stronger nations than you.
11.24: ‘Every place on which the sole of your foot treads is yours: from the wilderness, and Leḇanon, from the river, the River Perath, even to the Western Sea is your border.
11.25: ‘No man shall stand against you. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall put the dread of you and the fear of you upon all the land where you tread, as He has spoken to you.
11.26: ‘See, I am putting before you today a beraḵah and a curse:
11.27: the beraḵah, when you obey the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim which I command you today;
11.28: and the curse, if you do not obey the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, but turn aside from the Way which I command you today, to go after other mighty ones which you have not known.
11.29: ‘And it shall be, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has brought you into the land which you go to possess, that you shall put the beraḵah on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ĕyḇal.
11.30: ‘Are they not beyond the Yardĕn, following the way of the sun westward, in the land of the Kena’anites who dwell in the desert plain opposite Gilgal, beside the terebinth trees of Moreh?
11.31: ‘For you are passing over the Yardĕn to go in to possess the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you, and you shall possess it and dwell in it,
11.32: and shall guard to do all the Laws and Right-Rulings which I am putting before you today.’

12.1: “These are the Laws and Right-Rulings which you guard to do in the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of your fathers is giving you to possess, all the days that you live on the land.
12.2: “Completely destroy all the places where the nations which you are dispossessing served their mighty ones, on the high mountains and on the hills and under every green tree.
12.3: “And you shall break down their altars, and destroy their pillars, and burn their Ashĕrim with fire. And you shall cut down the carved images of their mighty ones and shall destroy their name out of that place.
12.4: “Do not do so to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim,
12.5: but seek the place which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim chooses, out of all your tribes, to put His Name there, for His Dwelling Place, and there you shall enter.
12.6: “And there you shall take your burnt offerings, and your offerings, and your tithes, and the contributions of your hand, and your vowed offerings, and your voluntary offerings, and the firstlings of your herd and of your flock.
12.7: “And there you shall eat before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and shall rejoice in all that you put your hand to, you and your households, in which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has baraḵ you.
12.8: “Do not do all that we do here today - each one whatever is right in his own eyes.
12.9: “Because you have not yet entered the rest and the inheritance which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you.
12.10: “But you shall pass over the Yardĕn, and shall dwell in the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you to inherit, and He shall give you rest from all your enemies round about, and you shall dwell in safety.
12.11: “And it shall be, that unto the place which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim chooses to make His Name dwell there, there you are to bring all that I command you: your burnt offerings, and your offerings, and your tithes, and the contributions of your hand, and all your choice offerings which you vow to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
12.12: “And you shall rejoice before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, you and your sons and your daughters, and your male servants and your female servants, and the Lĕwite who is within your gates, since he has no portion nor inheritance with you.
12.13: “Guard yourself that you do not offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see,
12.14: except in the place which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 chooses, in one of your tribes, there you are to offer your burnt offerings, and there you are to do all that I command you.
12.15: “Only, whatever your being desires you shall slaughter and eat, according to the beraḵah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim which He has given you, within all your gates. The unclean and the clean do eat of it, of the gazelle and the deer alike.
12.16: “Only, the blood you do not eat, pour it on the earth like water.
12.17: “You are not allowed to eat within your gates the tithe of your grain, or of your new wine, or of your oil, or of the firstlings of your herd or your flock, or of any of your offerings which you vow, or of your voluntary offerings, or of the contribution of your hand.
12.18: “But eat them before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, in the place which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim chooses, you and your son and your daughter, and your male servant and your female servant, and the Lĕwite who is within your gates. And you shall rejoice before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim in all that you put your hands to.
12.19: “Guard yourself that you do not forsake the Lĕwite as long as you live in your land.
12.20: “When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim enlarges your border as He has promised you, and you say, ‘Let me eat meat,’ because you long to eat meat, you eat as much meat as your being desires.
12.21: “When the place where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim chooses to put His Name is too far from you, then you shall slaughter from your herd and from your flock which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has given you, as I have commanded you, and you shall eat within your gates as much as your being desires.
12.22: “Only, as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so you are to eat of it. The unclean and the clean alike eat of it.
12.23: “Only, be firm not to eat the blood, for the blood is the life, do not eat the life with the meat.
12.24: “Do not eat it, you pour it on the earth like water.
12.25: “Do not eat it, that it might be well with you and your children after you, when you do what is right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
12.26: “Only, the qodesh gifts which you have, and your vowed offerings, you are to take up and go to the place which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 chooses.
12.27: “And you shall make your burnt offerings, the meat and the blood, on the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim. And the blood of your offerings is poured out on the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and you eat the meat.
12.28: “Guard, and obey all these Words which I command you, that it might be well with you and your children after you forever, when you do what is good and right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
12.29: “When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim cuts off from before you the nations which you go to dispossess, and you dispossess them and dwell in their land,
12.30: guard yourself that you are not ensnared to follow them, after they are destroyed from before you, and that you do not inquire about their mighty ones, saying, ‘How did these nations serve their mighty ones? And let me do so too.’
12.31: “Do not do so to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, for every abomination which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 hates they have done to their mighty ones, for they even burn their sons and daughters in the fire to their mighty ones.
12.32: “All the Words I am commanding you, guard to do it - do not add to it nor take away from it.

13.1: “When there arises among you a naḇi or a dreamer of dreams, and he shall give you a sign or a wonder,
13.2: and the sign or the wonder shall come true, of which he has spoken to you, saying, ‘Let us go after other mighty ones - which you have not known - and serve them,’
13.3: do not listen to the words of that naḇi or that dreamer of dreams, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is trying you to know whether you love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim with all your heart and with all your being.
13.4: “Walk after 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim and revere Him, and guard His Commands and obey His voice, and serve Him and cling to Him.
13.5: “And that naḇi or that dreamer of dreams is put to death, because he has spoken apostasy against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim - who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim and redeemed you from the house of bondage - to make you stray from the Way in which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim commanded you to walk. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst.
13.6: “When your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or your daughter, or the wife of your bosom, or your friend who is as your own being, entices you secretly, saying, ‘Let us go and serve other mighty ones’ - which you have not known, neither you nor your fathers,
13.7: of the mighty ones of the people which are all around you, near to you or far off from you, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth -
13.8: do not agree with him or listen to him, nor shall your eye pardon him, nor spare him or conceal him,
13.9: but you shall certainly kill him. Your hand is first against him to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people,
13.10: and you shall stone him with stones until he dies, because he sought to entice you away from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, from the house of bondage.
13.11: “And let all Yisra’ĕl hear and revere, and not again do any such evil matter as this in your midst.
13.12: “When you hear someone in one of your cities, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim gives you to dwell in, saying,
13.13: ‘Some men, sons of Beliya’al, have gone out of your midst and led the inhabitants of their city astray, saying, “Let us go and serve other mighty ones” ’ - which you have not known -
13.14: then you shall inquire, search out, and ask diligently. And see if the matter is true and established that this abomination was done in your midst,
13.15: you shall certainly smite the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, putting it under the ban, and all that is in it and its livestock, with the edge of the sword.
13.16: “And gather all its plunder into the middle of the street, and completely burn with fire the city and all its plunder, before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim. And it shall be a heap forever, never to be built again.
13.17: “And none of that which is put under the ban is to cling to your hand, so that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 turns from the fierceness of His displeasure and shall show you compassion, love you and increase you, as He swore to your fathers,
13.18: when you obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, to guard all His Commands which I command you today, to do what is right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.

14.1: “You are the children of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim. Do not cut yourselves nor shave the front of your head for the dead,
14.2: for you are a qodesh people to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has chosen you to be a people for Himself, a treasured possession above all the peoples who are on the face of the earth.
14.4: “These are the living creatures which you do eat: ox, sheep, and goat,
14.5: deer, and gazelle, and roebuck, and wild goat, and mountain goat, and antelope, and mountain sheep.
14.6: “And every beast that has a split hoof divided in two, chewing the cud, among the beasts, you do eat.
14.7: “But of those chewing the cud or those having a split hoof completely divided, you do not eat, such as these: the camel, and the hare, and the rabbit, for they chew the cud but do not have a split hoof, they are unclean for you.
14.8: “And the pig is unclean for you, because it has a split hoof, but does not chew the cud. You do not eat their flesh or touch their dead carcasses.
14.9: “These you do eat of all that are in the waters: all that have fins and scales you do eat.
14.10: “And whatever does not have fins and scales you do not eat, it is unclean for you.
14.12: but these you do not eat: the eagle, and the vulture, and the black vulture,
14.13: and the red kite, and the falcon, and the buzzard after their kinds,
14.14: and every raven after its kind,
14.15: and the ostrich, and the nighthawk, and the seagull, and the hawk after their kinds,
14.16: the little owl, and the great owl, and the white owl,
14.17: and the pelican, and the carrion vulture, and the fisher owl,
14.18: and the stork, and the heron after its kind, and the hoopoe and the bat.
14.19: “And every creeping creature that flies is unclean for you, they are not eaten.
14.21: “Do not eat whatever dies of itself. Give it to the stranger who is within your gates, to eat it, or sell it to a foreigner. For you are a qodesh people to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim. Do not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.
14.22: “You shall tithe without fail all the yield of your grain that the field brings forth year by year.
14.23: “And you shall eat before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, in the place where He chooses to make His Name dwell, the tithe of your grain and your new wine and your oil, and of the firstlings of your herds and your sheep, so that you learn to revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim always.
14.24: “But when the way is too long for you, so that you are not able to bring the tithe, or when the place where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim chooses to put His Name is too far from you, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim baraḵ you,
14.25: then you shall give it in silver, and shall take the silver in your hand and go to the place which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim chooses.
14.26: “And you shall use the silver for whatever your being desires: for cattle or sheep, for wine or strong drink, for whatever your being desires. And you shall eat there before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and you shall rejoice, you and your household.
14.27: “And do not forsake the Lĕwite who is within your gates, for he has no part nor inheritance with you.
14.28: “At the end of every third year you bring out all the tithe of your increase of that year and store it up within your gates.
14.29: “And the Lĕwite, because he has no portion nor inheritance with you, and the sojourner and the fatherless and the widow who are within your gates, shall come and eat and be satisfied, so that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim baraḵ you in all the work of your hand which you do.

15.1: “At the end of every seven years you make a release of debts.
15.2: “And this is the word of the release: Every creditor is to release what he has loaned to his neighbor, he does not require it of his neighbor or his brother, because it is called the release of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.3: “Of a foreigner you could require it, but your hand is to release whatever is owed by your brother.
15.4: “Only, there should be no poor among you. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 greatly baraḵ you in the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you to possess as an inheritance,
15.5: only if you diligently obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, to guard to do all these Commands which I am commanding you today.
15.6: “For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall baraḵ you as He promised you. And you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow. And you shall rule over many nations, but they do not rule over you.
15.7: “When there is a poor man with you, one of your brothers, within any of the gates in your land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you, do not harden your heart nor shut your hand from your poor brother,
15.8: for you shall certainly open your hand to him and certainly lend him enough for his need, whatever he needs.
15.9: “Be on guard lest there be a thought of Beliya’al in your heart, saying, ‘The seventh year, the year of release, is near,’ and your eye is evil against your poor brother and you give him naught. And he shall cry out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 against you, and it shall be a sin in you.
15.10: “You shall certainly give to him, and your heart should not be grieved when you give to him, because for this reason 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim baraḵ you in all your works and in all to which you put your hand.
15.11: “Because the poor one does not cease from the land, therefore I am commanding you, saying, ‘You shall certainly open your hand to your brother, to your poor and to your needy one, in your land.’
15.12: “When your brother is sold to you, an Iḇri man or an Iḇri woman, and shall serve you six years, then let him go free from you in the seventh year.
15.13: “And when you send him away free from you, let him not go away empty-handed.
15.14: “You shall richly supply him from your flock, and from your threshing-floor, and from your winepress. With that which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has baraḵ you with, give to him.
15.15: “And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Mitsrayim, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim redeemed you. Therefore I am commanding you this Word today.
15.16: “And it shall be, when he says to you, ‘I do not go away from you,’ because he loves you and your house, because it is good for him with you,
15.17: then you shall take an awl and thrust it through his ear to the door, and he shall be your servant forever. Do the same to your female servant.
15.18: “Let it not be hard in your eyes when you send him away free from you, for he has been worth a double hired servant in serving you six years. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall baraḵ you in all that you do.
15.19: “Qadosh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim all the first-born males that come from your herd and your flock. Do no work with the first-born of your herd, nor shear the first-born of your flock.
15.20: “You and your household are to eat it before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim year by year in the place which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 chooses.
15.21: “But when there is any defect in it, lame or blind, or has any evil defect, do not slaughter it to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
15.22: “Eat it within your gates - the unclean and the clean alike - as the gazelle, and as the deer.
15.23: “Only, do not eat its blood, pour it on the ground like water.

16.1: “Guard the month of Aḇiḇ, and perform the Pesaḥ to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, for in the month of Aḇiḇ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim brought you out of Mitsrayim by night.
16.2: “And you shall slaughter the Pesaḥ to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, from the flock and the herd, in the place where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 chooses to put His Name.
16.3: “Eat no leavened bread with it. For seven days you eat unleavened bread with it, bread of affliction, because you came out of the land of Mitsrayim in haste - so that you remember the day in which you came out of the land of Mitsrayim, all the days of your life.
16.4: “And no leaven should be seen with you in all your border for seven days, neither should the meat which you slaughter in the evening on the first day stay all night until morning.
16.5: “You are not allowed to slaughter the Pesaḥ within any of your gates which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim gives you,
16.6: but at the place where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim chooses to make His Name dwell, there you slaughter the Pesaḥ in the evening, at the going down of the sun, at the Appointed Time you came out of Mitsrayim.
16.7: “And you shall roast and eat it in the place which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim chooses, and in the morning you shall turn and go to your tents.
16.8: “Six days you eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there is a closing Festival to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim - you do no work.
16.9: “Count seven weeks for yourself. Begin to count seven weeks from the time you begin to put the sickle to the grain.
16.10: “And you shall perform the Festival of Shaḇuoth to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, according to the voluntary offering from your hand, which you give as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim baraḵ you.
16.11: “And you shall rejoice before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, you and your son and your daughter, and your male servant and your female servant, and the Lĕwite who is within your gates, and the stranger and the fatherless and the widow who is in your midst, at the place where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim chooses to make His Name dwell.
16.12: “And you shall remember that you were a slave in Mitsrayim, and you shall guard and do these Laws.
16.13: “Perform the Festival of Sukkoth for seven days after the ingathering from your threshing-floor and from your winepress,
16.14: and you shall rejoice in your Festival, you and your son and your daughter, and your male servant and your female servant, and the Lĕwite, and the stranger and the fatherless and the widow who are within your gates.
16.15: “For seven days you shall celebrate a Festival to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim in the place which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 chooses, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim baraḵ you in all your increase and in all the work of your hands, and you shall be only rejoicing!
16.16: “Three times a year all your males appear before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim in the place which He chooses: at the Festival of Matstsoth, and at the Festival of Shaḇuoth, and at the Festival of Sukkoth. And none should appear before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 empty-handed,
16.17: each one with the gift of his hand, according to the beraḵah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim which He has given you.
16.18: “Appoint judges and officers within all your gates, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you, according to your tribes. And they shall judge the people with righteous right-ruling.
16.19: “Do not distort right-ruling. Do not show partiality, nor take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.
16.20: “Follow righteousness, righteousness so that you live and inherit the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you.
16.21: “Do not plant for yourself any tree as an Ashĕrah near the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim that you make for yourself.
16.22: “And do not put up a pillar, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim hates.

17.1: “Do not slaughter to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim a bull or sheep which has any blemish, any evil matter, for that is an abomination to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
17.2: “When there is found in your midst, in any of your cities which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you, a man or a woman who does what is evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, in transgressing His Covenant,
17.3: and has gone and served other mighty ones and bowed down to them, or to the sun or to the moon or to any of the host of the shamayim, which I have not commanded,
17.4: and it has been made known to you and you have heard, and have searched diligently. Then see, if true: the matter is confirmed that such an abomination has been done in Yisra’ĕl,
17.5: then you shall bring out to your gates that man or woman who has done this evil matter, and you shall stone to death that man or woman with stones.
17.6: “At the mouth of two or three witnesses shall he that is to die be put to death. He is not put to death by the mouth of one witness.
17.7: “The hand of the witnesses shall be first against him to put him to death, and the hand of all the people last. So you shall purge the evil from your midst.
17.8: “When any matter arises which is too hard for you to judge, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, or between stroke and stroke - matters of strife within your gates - then you shall rise and go up to the place which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim chooses,
17.9: and shall come to the kohenim, the Lĕwites, and to the judge who is in those days, and shall inquire. And they shall declare to you the word of Right-Ruling,
17.10: and you shall do according to the word which they declare to you from that place which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 chooses. And you shall guard to do according to all that they instruct you.
17.11: “Do according to the Torah in which they teach you, according to the Right-Ruling which they say to you. You do not turn to the right or to the left from the word which they declare to you.
17.12: “And the man who acts arrogantly, so as not to listen to the kohĕn who stands to serve there before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, or to the judge, that man shall die. So you shall purge the evil from Yisra’ĕl.
17.13: “And let all the people hear and revere, and no longer do arrogantly.
17.14: “When you come to the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you, and shall possess it and shall dwell in it, and you shall say, ‘Let me appoint a meleḵ over me like all the gentiles that are around me,’
17.15: you shall certainly appoint meleḵ over you whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall choose. Appoint a meleḵ over you from among your brothers, you are not allowed to appoint a foreigner over you, who is not your brother.
17.16: “Only, he is not to increase horses for himself, nor cause the people to return to Mitsrayim to increase horses, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has said to you, ‘Do not return that way again.’
17.17: “And he is not to increase wives for himself, lest his heart turn away, nor is he to greatly increase silver and gold for himself.
17.18: “And it shall be, when he sits on the throne of his reign, that he shall write for himself a copy of this Torah in a book, from the one before the kohenim, the Lĕwites.
17.19: “And it shall be with him, and he shall read it all the days of his life, so that he learns to revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim and guard all the Words of this Torah and these Laws, to do them,
17.20: so that his heart is not lifted up above his brothers, and so as not to turn aside from the Command, right or left, so that he prolongs his days in his reign, he and his children, in the midst of Yisra’ĕl.

18.1: “The kohenim, the Lĕwites, all the tribe of Lĕwi, have no part nor inheritance with Yisra’ĕl. They are to eat the offerings of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 made by fire, and His inheritance.
18.2: “But among his brothers, no inheritance. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is his inheritance, as He has spoken to him.
18.3: “And this is the kohĕn’s right from the people, from those who bring an offering, whether it is bull or sheep: they shall give to the kohĕn the shoulder, and the two cheeks, and the stomach;
18.4: the first-fruits of your grain and your new wine and your oil, and the first of the fleece of your sheep, you give to him.
18.5: “For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has chosen him out of all your tribes to stand to serve in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, him and his sons forever.
18.6: “And when the Lĕwite comes from one of your gates, from where he has sojourned among all Yisra’ĕl, and shall come with all the desire of his being to the place which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 chooses,
18.7: then he shall serve in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim, like all his brothers the Lĕwites, who are standing there before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
18.8: “They are to have portion for portion to eat, besides what comes from the sale of his inheritance.
18.9: “When you come into the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you, do not learn to do according to the abominations of those gentiles.
18.10: “Let no one be found among you who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire, or one who practices divination, or a user of magic, or one who interprets omens or a sorcerer,
18.11: or one who conjures spells, or a medium, or a spiritist, or one who calls up the dead.
18.12: “For whoever does these are an abomination to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and because of these abominations 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim drives them out from before you.
18.14: for these nations whom you are dispossessing listen to those using magic and to diviners. But as for you, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has not appointed such for you.
18.15: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall raise up for you a Naḇi like me from your midst, from your brothers. Listen to Him,
18.16: according to all you asked of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim in Ḥorĕḇ in the day of the assembly, saying, ‘Let me not hear again the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim, nor let me see this great fire any more, lest I die.’
18.17: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, ‘What they have spoken is good.
18.18: ‘I shall raise up for them a Naḇi like you out of the midst of their brothers. And I shall put My Words in His mouth, and He shall speak to them all that I command Him.
18.19: ‘And it shall be, the man who does not listen to My Words which He speaks in My Name, I require it of him.
18.20: ‘But the naḇi who presumes to speak a word in My Name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other mighty ones, even that naḇi shall die.’
18.21: “And when you say in your heart, ‘How do we know the word which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has not spoken?’ -
18.22: when the naḇi speaks in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and the word is not, or comes not, that is the word which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has not spoken. The naḇi has spoken it presumptuously. Do not be afraid of him.

19.1: “When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim cuts off the nations whose land 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you, and you dispossess them and dwell in their cities and in their houses,
19.2: separate three cities for yourself in the midst of your land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you to possess.
19.3: “Prepare a way for yourself, and divide into three parts the border of your land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you to inherit, that anyone who killed someone shall flee there.
19.4: “And this is the matter of the one who killed someone who flees there and live: He who smites his neighbor unintentionally, not having hated him in time past,
19.5: even he who goes to the forest with his neighbor to cut timber, and his hand swings a stroke with the axe to cut down the tree, and the head slips from the handle and strikes his neighbor so that he dies - let him flee to one of these cities and live,
19.6: lest the revenger of blood, while his displeasure is hot, pursue the one who killed someone and overtake him, because the way is long, and shall smite him, though he was not worthy of death, since he had not hated him before.
19.7: “Therefore I am commanding you, saying, ‘Separate three cities for yourself.’
19.8: “And if 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim enlarges your border, as He swore to your fathers, and has given you the land which He promised to give to your fathers -
19.9: when you guard all this Command to do it, which I am commanding you today, to love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim and to walk in His Ways all the days - then you shall add three more cities for yourself besides these three,
19.10: so that innocent blood is not shed in the midst of your land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you as an inheritance, or blood-guilt shall be upon you.
19.11: “But when anyone hates his neighbor, and shall lie in wait for him and rise against him and smite the life from him so that he dies, then he shall flee to one of these cities,
19.12: and the elders of his city shall send and bring him from there, and give him into the hand of the revenger of blood, and he shall die.
19.13: “Your eye shall not pardon him, but you shall purge the blood of the innocent from Yisra’ĕl, so that it might be well with you.
19.14: “Do not remove your neighbor’s boundary, which those in the past have bound, in your inheritance which you inherit in the land that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you to possess.
19.15: “One witness does not rise up against a man concerning any wickedness or any sin that he commits. At the mouth of two witnesses or at the mouth of three witnesses a matter is established.
19.16: “When a malicious witness rises up against any man to accuse him of turning aside,
19.17: then both men who have the dispute shall stand before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, before the kohenim and the judges who serve in those days.
19.18: “And the judges shall diligently search and see if the witness is a false witness, who has falsely accused his brother,
19.19: then you shall do to him as he thought to have done to his brother. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst.
19.20: “And let the rest hear and revere, and never again do this evil matter in your midst.
19.21: “And let your eye not pardon, life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

2.1: “Then we turned and departed into the wilderness, the way of the Sea of Reeds, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to me, and we went round Mount Sĕ’ir, many days.
2.3: ‘You have gone around this mountain long enough, turn northward.
2.4: ‘And command the people, saying, “You are about to pass over into the border of your brothers, the descendants of Ĕsaw, who live in Sĕ’ir, and they are afraid of you. So be on your guard.
2.5: “Do not strive with them, for I do not give you any of their land, no, not so much as one footstep, because I have given Mount Sĕ’ir to Ĕsaw as a possession.
2.6: “What food you buy from them with silver you shall eat. And also, what water you buy from them with silver you shall drink.
2.7: “For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has baraḵ you in all the work of your hand. He has known your wandering through this great wilderness. These forty years 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has been with you, you have not lacked any matter.” ’
2.8: “And when we passed beyond our brothers, the descendants of Ĕsaw who dwell in Sĕ’ir, away from the way of the desert plain, away from Ĕylath and Etsyon Geḇer, we turned and passed over by way of the Wilderness of Mo’aḇ.
2.9: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, ‘Do not distress Mo’aḇ, nor stir yourself up against them in battle, for I do not give you any of their land as a possession, because I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as a possession.’ ”
2.10: The Ĕymites had dwelt there formerly, a people as great and numerous and tall as the Anaqim.
2.11: They were also reckoned as Repha’ites, like the Anaqim, but the Mo’aḇites call them Ĕymites.
2.12: And the Ḥorites formerly dwelt in Sĕ’ir, but the descendants of Ĕsaw dispossessed them and destroyed them from before them, and dwelt in their place, as Yisra’ĕl did to the land of their possession which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 gave them.
2.13: “ ‘Now rise up, and pass over the wadi Zereḏ.’ So we passed over the wadi Zereḏ.
2.14: “And the time we took to come from Qaḏĕsh Barnĕa until we passed over the wadi Zereḏ was thirty-eight years, until all the generation of the men of battle was consumed from the midst of the camp, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had sworn to them.
2.15: “And also, the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was against them, to destroy them from the midst of the camp until they were consumed.
2.16: “And it came to be, when all the men of battle had finally perished from among the people,
2.17: that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to me, saying,
2.18: ‘This day you are to pass over at Ar, the boundary of Mo’aḇ.
2.19: ‘And when you come near the children of Ammon, do not distress them nor stir yourself up against them, for I do not give you any of the land of the children of Ammon as a possession, because I have given it to the descendants of Lot as a possession.’
2.20: That was also reckoned as a land of Repha’ites. Repha’ites formerly dwelt there. But the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,
2.21: a people as great and numerous and tall as the Anaqim. But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 destroyed them before them, and they dispossessed them and dwelt in their place,
2.22: as He had done for the descendants of Ĕsaw, who dwelt in Sĕ’ir, when He destroyed the Ḥorites from before them. They dispossessed them and dwelt in their place, even to this day.
2.23: And the Awwim who dwelt in villages as far as Azzah, the Kaphtorim who came from Kaphtor, destroyed them and dwelt in their place.
2.24: ‘Arise, depart and pass over the wadi Arnon. See, I have given into your hand Siḥon the Amorite, meleḵ of Ḥeshbon, and his land. Begin to possess it, and stir up yourself against him in battle.
2.25: ‘This day I begin to put the dread and fear of you upon the peoples under all the shamayim, who, when they hear the report of you, shall tremble and shake because of you.’
2.26: “Then I sent messengers from the Wilderness of Qeḏĕmoth to Siḥon meleḵ of Ḥeshbon, with words of peace, saying,
2.27: ‘Let me pass over through your land on the highway. I shall go on the highway and turn neither to the right nor to the left.
2.28: ‘What food you sell me for silver I shall eat, and what water you give me for silver I shall drink. Only let me pass over on foot,
2.29: as the descendants of Ĕsaw who dwell in Sĕ’ir and the Mo’aḇites who dwell in Ar did for me - until I pass over the Yardĕn to the land 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim is giving us.’
2.30: “But Siḥon meleḵ of Ḥeshbon would not let us pass over, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim hardened his spirit and strengthened his heart, to give him into your hand, as it is this day.
2.31: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, ‘See, I have begun to give Siḥon and his land over to you. Begin to possess - in order to possess his land.’
2.32: “And Siḥon and all his people came out against us to fight at Yahats,
2.33: and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim gave him over to us, so we smote him, and his sons, and all his people.
2.34: “And we took all his cities at that time, and we put the men, women, and little ones of every city under the ban, we left none remaining.
2.35: “Only the livestock we took as plunder for ourselves, and the spoil of the cities which we captured.
2.36: “From Aro’ĕr, which is on the edge of the wadi Arnon, and the city that is by the wadi, as far as Gil’aḏ, there was not one city too high for us. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim gave all to us.
2.37: “Only you did not go near the land of the children of Ammon - anywhere along the wadi Yabboq, or to the cities of the mountains, or wherever 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim had commanded us.

20.1: “When you go out to battle against your enemies, and shall see horses and chariots and people more numerous than you, do not be afraid of them, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, who brought you up from the land of Mitsrayim, is with you.
20.2: “And it shall be, when you draw near to the battle, that the kohĕn shall come and speak to the people,
20.3: and shall say to them, ‘Hear, O Yisra’ĕl: You are drawing near today to battle with your enemies. Do not let your heart faint, do not fear, or tremble, or be afraid before them,
20.4: for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is He who goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.’
20.5: “And the officers shall speak to the people, saying, ‘Who is the man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man dedicate it.
20.6: ‘And who is the man who has planted a vineyard and has not begun to use it? Let him also go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man should begin to use it.
20.7: ‘And who is the man who is engaged to a woman and has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her.’
20.8: “And the officers shall speak further to the people, and say, ‘Who is the man who is afraid and tender of heart? Let him go and return to his house, lest the heart of his brothers faint like his heart.’
20.9: “And it shall be, when the officers have finished speaking to the people, that they shall appoint commanders of the divisions to lead the people.
20.10: “When you draw near to a city to fight against it, then you shall make a call for peace to it.
20.11: “And it shall be that if it accepts your call for peace, and shall open to you, then all the people found in it are to be your compulsory labor, and serve you.
20.12: “But if it does not make peace with you, and shall fight against you, then you shall besiege it,
20.13: and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall give it into your hands, and you shall smite every male in it with the edge of the sword.
20.14: “Only the women, and the little ones, and the livestock, and all that is in the city, all its spoil, you take as plunder for yourself. And you shall eat the enemies’ plunder which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim gives you.
20.15: “Do so to all the cities which are very far from you, which are not of the cities of these nations.
20.16: “Only, of the cities of these peoples which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim gives you as an inheritance, you do not keep alive any that breathe,
20.17: but you shall certainly put them under the ban: the Ḥittite and the Amorite and the Kena’anite and the Perizzite and the Ḥiwwite and the Yeḇusite, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has commanded you,
20.18: lest they teach you to do according to all their abominations which they have done for their mighty ones, and you sin against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
20.19: “When you besiege a city for a long time by fighting against it to take it, you do not destroy its trees by wielding an axe against them. If you do eat of them, do not cut them down. For is the tree of the field a man to be besieged by you?
20.20: “Only the trees which you know are not trees for food you do destroy and cut down, to build siege-works against the city that is fighting against you, until it falls.

21.1: “When anyone is found slain, lying in the field in the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you to possess, and it is not known who smote him,
21.2: then your elders and your judges shall go out, and they shall measure the distance from the slain man to the cities round about.
21.3: “And it shall be that the elders of the city nearest to the slain man shall take a heifer which has not been worked and which has not pulled with a yoke,
21.4: and the elders of that city shall bring the heifer down to a wadi with flowing water, which is neither ploughed nor sown, and they shall break the heifer’s neck there in the wadi.
21.5: “And the kohenim, the sons of Lĕwi, shall come near, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has chosen them to serve Him and to baraḵ in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and by their command every strife and every stroke.
21.6: “And let all the elders of that city nearest to the slain man wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the wadi.
21.7: “And they shall answer and say, ‘Our hands have not shed this blood, nor have our eyes seen it.
21.8: ‘O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, forgive Your people Yisra’ĕl, whom You have redeemed, and do not allow innocent blood in the midst of Your people Yisra’ĕl.’ And the blood-guilt shall be pardoned to them.
21.9: “Thus you purge the guilt of innocent blood from your midst when you do what is right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
21.10: “When you go out to fight against your enemies, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall give them into your hand, and you shall take them captive,
21.11: and shall see among the captives a woman lovely of form, and shall delight in her and take her for your wife,
21.12: then you shall bring her home to your house, and she shall shave her head and trim her nails,
21.13: and put aside the mantle of her captivity, and shall dwell in your house, and mourn her father and her mother a month of days. And after that you shall go in to her and be her husband, and she shall be your wife.
21.14: “And it shall be, if you are not pleased with her, then you shall let her go at her desire, but you do not sell her at all for silver. Do not treat her harshly, since you have humbled her.
21.15: “When a man has two wives, one loved and the other unloved, and they have borne him children, both the loved and the unloved, and the first-born son is of her who is unloved,
21.16: then it shall be, on the day he makes his sons to inherit his possessions, he is not allowed to treat the son of the beloved wife as first-born in the face of the son of the unloved, who is the first-born.
21.17: “But he is to acknowledge the son of the unloved wife as the first-born by giving him a double portion of all that he has, for he is the beginning of his strength - the right of the first-born is his.
21.18: “When a man has a wayward and rebellious son who is not listening to the voice of his father or the voice of his mother, and who, when they have disciplined him, does not listen to them,
21.19: then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his city, to the gate of his city,
21.20: and shall say to the elders of his city, ‘This son of ours is wayward and rebellious. He is not listening to our voice, he is a glutton and a drunkard.’
21.21: “Then all the men of his city shall stone him to death with stones. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst. And let all Yisra’ĕl hear, and revere.
21.22: “And when a man has committed a sin worthy of death, then he shall be put to death and you shall hang him on a tree.
21.23: “Let his body not remain overnight on the tree, for you shall certainly bury him the same day - for he who is hanged is accursed of Elohim - so that you do not defile the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you as an inheritance.

22.1: “When you see your brother’s ox or his sheep going astray, you shall not hide yourself from them. Return them to your brother without fail.
22.2: “And if your brother is not near you, or if you do not know him, then you shall bring it to your own house, and it shall be with you until your brother seeks it, then you shall return it to him.
22.3: “And so you do with his donkey, and so you do with his garment, and so you do with whatever your brother loses, which he has lost and you have found. You are not allowed to hide yourself.
22.4: “When you see your brother’s donkey or his ox fall down on the way, you shall not hide yourself from them. Help him raise them without fail.
22.5: “A woman does not wear that which pertains to a man, nor does a man put on a woman’s garment, for whoever does this is an abomination to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
22.6: “When you come upon a bird’s nest along the way, in any tree or on the ground, with young ones or eggs, with the mother sitting on the young or on the eggs, do not take the mother with the young -
22.7: let the mother go without fail, and take the young for yourself, so that it might be well with you, and that you have prolonged days.
22.8: “When you build a new house, then you shall make a parapet for your roof, so that you do not bring blood-guilt on your house when one falls from it.
22.9: “Do not sow your vineyard with different kinds of seed, lest the yield of the seed which you have sown and the fruit of your vineyard be defiled.
22.10: “Do not plough with an ox and a donkey together.
22.11: “Do not put on a garment of different kinds, of wool and linen together.
22.12: “Make tassels on the four corners of the garment with which you cover yourself.
22.13: “When any man takes a wife, and shall go in to her, and shall hate her,
22.14: and shall make abusive charges against her and bring an evil name on her and say, ‘I took this woman, and when I came to her I did not find her a maiden,’
22.15: then the father and mother of the young woman shall take and bring out the proof of the girl’s maidenhood to the elders of the city at the gate.
22.16: “And the girl’s father shall say to the elders, ‘I gave my daughter to this man as wife, and he hates her.
22.17: ‘And see, he has made abusive charges against her, saying, “I did not find your daughter a maiden,” and yet these are the proofs of my daughter’s maidenhood.’ And they shall spread the garment before the elders of the city.
22.18: “And the elders of that city shall take that man and punish him,
22.19: and fine him one hundred pieces of silver and give them to the father of the young woman, because he has brought an evil name on a maiden of Yisra’ĕl. And she is to be his wife, he is not allowed to put her away all his days.
22.20: “But if the matter is true, that the girl was not found a maiden,
22.21: then they shall bring out the girl to the door of her father’s house, and the men of her city shall stone her to death with stones, because she has done wickedness in Yisra’ĕl, to whore in her father’s house. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst.
22.22: “When a man is found lying with a woman married to a husband, then both of them shall die, both the man that lay with the woman, and the woman. Thus you shall purge the evil from Yisra’ĕl.
22.23: “When a girl who is a maiden is engaged to a husband, and a man finds her in the city and lies with her,
22.24: then you shall bring them both out to the gate of that city, and shall stone them to death with stones, the girl because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he has humbled his neighbor’s wife. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst.
22.25: “But if a man finds the girl who is engaged in the field, and the man seizes her and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die.
22.26: “But you shall do no matter to the girl. The girl has no sin worthy of death - for the matter is like a man who rises against his neighbor and kills him -
22.27: for he found her in the field, and she cried out the engaged girl, but without anyone to save her.
22.28: “When a man finds a girl who is a maiden who is not engaged, and he seizes her and lies with her, and they are found out,
22.29: then the man who lay with her shall give to the girl’s father fifty pieces of silver, and she is to be his wife because he has humbled her. He is not allowed to put her away all his days.
22.30: “A man does not take his father’s wife, nor uncover his father’s skirt.

23.1: “One of wounded, mutilated or genitalia cut off, does not enter the assembly of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.2: “One of incestuous birth does not enter the assembly of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, even a tenth generation of his does not enter the assembly of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.3: “An Ammonite or Mo’aḇite does not enter the assembly of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, even a tenth generation of them does not ever enter the assembly of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
23.4: because they did not meet you with bread and water on the way when you came out of Mitsrayim, and because they hired against you Bil’am son of Be’or from Pethor of Aram Naharayim, to curse you.
23.5: “But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim refused to listen to Bil’am, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim turned the curse into a beraḵah for you, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim loves you.
23.6: “Do not seek their peace nor their good, all your days, forever.
23.7: “Do not loathe an Eḏomite, for he is your brother. Do not loathe a Mitsrite, because you were a stranger in his land.
23.8: “The children of the third generation born to them do enter the assembly of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.9: “When the army goes out against your enemies, then you shall guard yourself from every evil matter.
23.10: “When there is any man among you who is not clean because of an emission in the night, then he shall go outside the camp. Let him not come into the midst of the camp.
23.11: “And it shall be, toward evening, that he bathes with water. And when the sun goes let him come into the midst of the camp.
23.12: “And you shall have a place outside the camp, where you shall go out,
23.13: and you shall have a sharp implement among your equipment, and when you sit down outside, you shall dig with it and turn and cover your excrement.
23.14: “For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim walks in the midst of your camp, to deliver you and give your enemies over to you. Therefore your camp shall be qodesh, so that He does not see unclean matter among you, and shall turn away from you.
23.15: “You do not hand over to his master the slave who has escaped from his master to you.
23.16: “Let him dwell with you in your midst, in the place which he chooses within one of your gates, where it is pleasing to him. Do not oppress him.
23.17: “None of the daughters of Yisra’ĕl is to be a cult prostitute, nor any of the sons of Yisra’ĕl be a cult prostitute.
23.18: “Do not bring the hire of a whore or the pay of a dog to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim for any vowed offering, for both of these are an abomination to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
23.19: “Do not lend at interest to your brother, interest of silver, interest of food, or interest of whatever is lent at interest.
23.20: “To a foreigner you lend at interest, but to your brother you do not lend at interest, so that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim might baraḵ you in all that you put your hand to in the land which you are entering to possess.
23.21: “When you make a vow to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, do not delay to pay it, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is certainly requiring it of you, and it shall be sin in you.
23.22: “But when you abstain from vowing, it is not sin in you.
23.23: “That which has gone from your lips you shall guard and do, for you voluntarily vowed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim what you have promised with your mouth.
23.24: “When you come into your neighbor’s vineyard, you shall eat to the satisfaction of your desire, but do not put any in a receptacle of yours.
23.25: “When you come into your neighbor’s standing grain, you shall pluck the heads with your hand, but do not use a sickle on your neighbor’s standing grain.

24.1: “When a man takes a wife and shall marry her, then it shall be, if she finds no favor in his eyes because he has found a matter of shamefulness in her, and he shall write her a certificate of divorce, and put it in her hand, and send her out of his house,
24.2: and if she left his house and went and became another man’s wife,
24.3: and the latter husband shall hate her and write her a certificate of divorce, and put it in her hand, and send her out of his house, or when the latter husband dies who took her to be his wife,
24.4: then her former husband who sent her away is not allowed to take her back to be his wife after she has been defiled, for that would be an abomination before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And do not bring sin on the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you as an inheritance.
24.5: “When a man has taken a new wife, let him not go out into the army nor let any matter be imposed upon him. He shall be exempt one year for the sake of his home, to rejoice with his wife whom he has taken.
24.6: “No one takes in pledge the lower or the upper millstone, for he would be taking a life in pledge.
24.7: “When a man is found kidnapping any of his brothers of the children of Yisra’ĕl, and treats him harshly or sells him, then that kidnapper shall die. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst.
24.8: “Take heed, in an outbreak of leprosy, to diligently guard and do according to all that the kohenim, the Lĕwites, teach you. As I have commanded them, so you shall guard to do.
24.9: “Remember what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim did to Miryam on the way when you came out of Mitsrayim.
24.10: “When you lend your brother a loan, do not go into his house to get his pledge.
24.11: “Stand outside, and let the man to whom you lend bring the pledge out to you.
24.12: “And if the man is poor, do not sleep with his pledge.
24.13: “By all means return the pledge to him at sundown, and he shall sleep in his own garment, and shall baraḵ you. And it shall be righteousness to you before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
24.14: “Do not oppress a hired servant who is poor and needy, of your brothers or of the strangers who is in your land within your gates.
24.15: “Give him his wages on the same day, and do not let the sun go down on it, for he is poor and lifts up his being to it, so that he does not cry out against you to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and it shall be sin in you.
24.16: “Fathers are not put to death for their children, and children are not put to death for their fathers, each is to die for his own sin.
24.17: “Do not twist the right-ruling of a stranger or the fatherless, nor take the garment of a widow.
24.18: “But you shall remember that you were a slave in Mitsrayim, and that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim redeemed you from there. Therefore I am commanding you to do this Word.
24.19: “When you reap your harvest in your field, and have forgotten a sheaf in the field, do not go back to get it. Let it be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow, so that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim might baraḵ you in all the work of your hands.
24.20: “When you beat your olive trees, do not examine the branch behind you. Let it be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
24.21: “When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, do not glean behind you. Let it be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
24.22: “And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Mitsrayim. Therefore I am commanding you to do this Word.

25.1: “When there is a dispute between men, then they shall come unto judgment, and they shall be judged, and the righteous declared righteous and the wicked declared wicked.
25.2: “And it shall be, if the wicked is to be beaten, that the judge shall cause him to lie down and be beaten in his presence with the number of blows according to his wickedness.
25.3: “Forty blows he gives him but no more, lest he beat him with many more blows than these, and your brother be degraded before your eyes.
25.4: “Do not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.
25.5: “When brothers dwell together, and one of them has died, and has no son, the widow of the dead man shall not become a stranger’s outside. Her husband’s brother goes in to her, and shall take her as his wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother to her.
25.6: “And it shall be that the first-born son which she bears rises up for the name of his dead brother, so that his name is not blotted out of Yisra’ĕl.
25.7: “But if the man does not desire to take his brother’s wife, then let his brother’s wife go up to the gate to the elders, and say, ‘My husband’s brother refuses to raise up a name to his brother in Yisra’ĕl, he does not agree to perform the duty of my husband’s brother.’
25.8: “The elders of his city shall then call him and speak to him, and he shall stand and say, ‘I have no desire to take her,’
25.9: then his brother’s wife shall come to him in the presence of the elders, and remove his sandal from his foot, and shall spit in his face, and answer and say, ‘Thus it is done to the man who does not build up his brother’s house.’
25.10: “And in Yisra’ĕl his name shall be called, ‘The house of him who had his sandal removed.’
25.11: “When men fight together, a man with another, and the wife of one shall draw near to rescue her husband from the hand of the one attacking him, and shall put out her hand and seize him by the genitals,
25.12: then you shall cut off her hand - your eye does not pardon.
25.13: “You shall not have in your bag differing weights, a heavy and a light.
25.14: “You shall not have in your house differing measures, a large and a small.
25.15: “You shall have a perfect and right weight, a perfect and right measure, so that they prolong your days on the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you.
25.16: “For all who do these, and all who do unrighteously, are an abomination to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
25.17: “Remember what Amalĕq did to you on the way as you were coming out of Mitsrayim,
25.18: how he met you on the way and attacked your back, all the feeble ones in your rear, when you were tired and weary. And he did not revere Elohim.
25.19: “Therefore it shall be, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has given you rest from your enemies all around, in the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you to possess as an inheritance, that you blot out the remembrance of Amalĕq from under the shamayim. Do not forget!

26.1: “And it shall be, when you come into the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you as an inheritance, and you possess it and dwell in it,
26.2: that you shall take some of the first of all the fruits of the land which you bring from your land that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you, and shall put it in a basket and go to the place where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim chooses to make His Name dwell there.
26.3: “And you shall come to the one who is kohĕn in those days, and say to him, ‘I shall declare today to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim that I have come to the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 swore to our fathers to give us.’
26.4: “And the kohĕn shall take the basket from your hand and place it before the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
26.5: “And you shall answer and say before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, ‘My father was a perishing Aramean, and he went down to Mitsrayim and sojourned there with few men. And there he became a nation, great, mighty, and numerous.
26.6: ‘But the Mitsrites did evil to us, and afflicted us, and imposed hard labor on us.
26.7: ‘Then we cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of our fathers, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 heard our voice and saw our affliction and our toil and our oppression.
26.8: ‘And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 brought us out of Mitsrayim with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm, with great reverence and with signs and wonders.
26.9: ‘And He brought us to this place and has given us this land, “a land flowing with milk and honey.”
26.10: ‘And now, see, I have brought the first-fruits of the land which You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, have given me.’ Then you shall place it before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and bow down before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim,
26.11: and shall rejoice in all the good which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has given to you and your house, you and the Lĕwite and the stranger who is among you.
26.12: “When you have completed tithing all the tithe of your increase in the third year, which is the year of tithing, and have given it to the Lĕwite, to the stranger, to the fatherless, and to the widow, and they have eaten within your gates and have been satisfied,
26.13: then you shall say before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, ‘I have put away the qodesh portion from my house, and also have given it to the Lĕwite, and to the stranger, and to the fatherless, and to the widow, according to all Your Command which You have commanded me. I have not transgressed Your Commands, nor have I forgotten.
26.14: ‘I have not eaten any of it when in mourning, nor have I removed any of it for any unclean use, nor given any of it for the dead. I have obeyed the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim, I have done according to all that You have commanded me.
26.15: ‘Look from Your qodesh dwelling place, from the shamayim, and baraḵ Your people Yisra’ĕl and the land which You have given us, as You swore to our fathers, “a land flowing with milk and honey.” ’
26.16: “Today 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is commanding you to do these Laws and Right-Rulings. And you shall guard and do them with all your heart and with all your being.
26.17: “You have today caused 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to proclaim to be your Elohim, and to walk in His Ways and guard His Laws, and His Commands, and His Right-Rulings, and to obey His voice.
26.18: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has caused you to proclaim today to be His people, a treasured possession, as He has spoken to you, and to guard all His Commands,
26.19: so as to make you high above all nations which He has made, for a praise, and for a name, and for esteem, and for you to be a qodesh people to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, as He has spoken.”

27.1: And Mosheh, with the elders of Yisra’ĕl, commanded the people, saying, “Guard all the Commands which I am commanding you today.
27.2: “And it shall be, on the day when you pass over the Yardĕn to the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you, that you shall put up for yourselves large stones, and plaster them with plaster,
27.3: and write on them all the Words of this Torah, when you have passed over, so that you go into the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you, ‘a land flowing with milk and honey,’ as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of your fathers has spoken to you.
27.4: “And it shall be, when you have passed over the Yardĕn, that on Mount Ĕyḇal you put up these stones, which I command you today, and you shall plaster them with plaster,
27.5: and build an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim there, an altar of stones - do not use an iron tool on them.
27.6: “Build the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim with complete stones, and you shall offer burnt offerings on it to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim,
27.7: and shall offer peace offerings, and eat there, and rejoice before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
27.8: “And you shall write all the Words of this Torah on the stones - plainly and well.”
27.9: And Mosheh and the kohenim, the Lĕwites, spoke to all Yisra’ĕl, saying, “Be silent and hear, O Yisra’ĕl: This day you have become the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim,
27.10: and you shall obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and do His Commands and His Laws which I command you today.”
27.11: And Mosheh commanded people on that day, saying,
27.12: “These are to stand on Mount Gerizim to baraḵ the people, when you have passed over the Yardĕn: Shim’on, and Lĕwi, and Yahuḏah, and Yissasḵar, and Yosĕph, and Binyamin.
27.13: “And these are to stand on Mount Ĕyḇal to curse: Re’uḇĕn, Gaḏ, and Ashĕr, and Zeḇulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
27.14: “And the Lĕwites shall speak with a loud voice and say to all the men of Yisra’ĕl:
27.15: ‘Cursed is the man who makes a carved or molded image, an abomination to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and puts it up in secret.’ And all the people shall answer and say, ‘Amĕn!’
27.16: ‘Cursed is he who makes light of his father or his mother.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’
27.17: ‘Cursed is he who moves his neighbor’s boundary.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’
27.18: ‘Cursed is he who misleads the blind in the way.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’
27.19: ‘Cursed is he who twists the right ruling of the stranger, the fatherless, and widow.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’
27.20: ‘Cursed is he who lies with his father’s wife, because he has uncovered his father’s bed.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’
27.21: ‘Cursed is he who lies with any beast.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’
27.22: ‘Cursed is he who lies with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’
27.23: ‘Cursed is he who lies with his mother-in-law.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’
27.24: ‘Cursed is he who smites his neighbor secretly.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’
27.25: ‘Cursed is he who takes a bribe to slay an innocent being.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’
27.26: ‘Cursed is he who does not establish the Words of this Torah.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’

28.1: “And it shall be, if you diligently obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, to guard to do all His Commands which I command you today, that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall make you high above all nations of the earth.
28.2: “And all these bireḵoth shall come upon you and overtake you, if you obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim:
28.3: “Baruḵ are you in the city, and baruḵ are you in the field.
28.4: “Baruḵ is the fruit of your body, and the fruit of your ground and the fruit of your livestock - the increase of your cattle and the offspring of your flocks.
28.5: “Baruḵ is your basket and your kneading bowl.
28.6: “Baruḵ are you when you come in, and baruḵ are you when you go out.
28.7: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 causes your enemies who rise against you to be smitten before your face - they come out against you one way and flee before you seven ways.
28.8: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commands the beraḵah on you in your storehouses and in all to which you put your hand, and shall baraḵ you in the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you.
28.9: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 establishes you as a qodesh people to Himself, as He has sworn to you, if you guard the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim and walk in His Ways.
28.10: “And all peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is called upon you, and they shall be afraid of you.
28.11: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall make you to have plenty of what is good, in the fruit of your body, in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your ground, in the land of which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 swore to your fathers to give you.
28.12: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 opens to you His good treasure, the shamayim, to give the rain to your land in its season, and to baraḵ all the work of your hand. And you shall lend to many nations, but you do not borrow.
28.13: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall make you the head and not the tail. And you shall be only on top, and not be beneath, if you obey the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, which I command you today, to guard and do.
28.14: “And do not turn aside from any of the Words which I am commanding you today, right or left, to go after other mighty ones to serve them.
28.15: “And it shall be, if you do not obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, to guard to do all His Commands and His Laws which I command you today, that all these curses shall come upon you and overtake you:
28.16: “Cursed are you in the city, and cursed are you in the field.
28.17: “Cursed is your basket and your kneading bowl.
28.18: “Cursed is the fruit of your body and the fruit of your land, the increase of your cattle and the offspring of your flocks.
28.19: “Cursed are you when you come in, and cursed are you when you go out.
28.20: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sends on you the curse, the confusion, and the rebuke in all that you put your hand to do, until you are destroyed and until you perish quickly, because of the evil of your doings by which you have forsaken Me.
28.21: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 makes the plague cling to you until He has consumed you from the land which you are going to possess.
