28.22: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 smites you with wasting disease, and with inflammation, and with burning, and with extreme heat, and with the sword, and with blight, and with mildew. And they shall pursue you until you perish.
28.23: “And your shamayim which are over your head shall be bronze, and the earth which is under you iron.
28.24: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 makes the rain of your land powder and dust; from the shamayim it comes down on you until you are destroyed.
28.25: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 causes you to be defeated before your enemies - you go out one way against them and flee seven ways before them. And you shall become a horror to all the reigns of the earth.
28.26: “And your carcasses shall be food for all the birds of the shamayim and the beasts of the earth, with no one to frighten them away.
28.27: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall smite you with the boils of Mitsrayim, with tumors, with the scab, and with the itch, from which you are unable to be healed.
28.28: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall smite you with madness and blindness and bewilderment of heart.
28.29: “And you shall be groping at noon, as a blind man gropes in darkness, and not prosper in your ways. And you shall be only oppressed and plundered all the days, with no one to save you.
28.30: “You become engaged to a wife, but another man lies with her. You build a house, but do not dwell in it. You plant a vineyard, but do not use its fruit.
28.31: “Your ox is slaughtered before your eyes, but you do not eat of it. Your donkey is violently taken from before you, and it is not given back to you. Your sheep are given to your enemies, with no one to save them.
28.32: “Your sons and your daughters are given to another people, and your eyes look and fail for them all day long, and your hand powerless.
28.33: “A people whom you have not known eat the fruit of your land and all your labors. And you shall be only oppressed and crushed all the days.
28.34: “And you shall be maddened because of the sight which your eyes see.
28.35: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 smites you in the knees and on the legs with evil boils of which you are unable to be healed, and from the sole of your foot to the top of your head.
28.36: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 brings you and the meleḵ whom you appoint over you to a nation which neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you shall serve other mighty ones, wood and stone.
28.37: “Thus you shall become an astonishment, a proverb, and a mockery among all the peoples to which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 drives you.
28.38: “You take much seed out into the field but gather little in, for the locust consumes it.
28.39: “You plant vineyards, and shall labor, but you neither drink of the wine nor gather, for the worm eats it.
28.40: “You have olive trees in all your border, but do not anoint with oil, for your olives drop off.
28.41: “You bring forth sons and daughters, but they are not with you, for they go into captivity.
28.42: “Locusts possess all your trees and the fruit of your ground.
28.43: “The sojourner who is among you rises higher and higher above you, but you come down lower and lower.
28.44: “He lends to you, but you do not lend to him. He is the head, and you are the tail.
28.45: “And all these curses shall come upon you, and they shall pursue and overtake you, until you are destroyed, because you did not obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, to guard His Commands and His Laws which He commanded you.
28.46: “And they shall be upon you for a sign and for a wonder, and on your seed, forever,
28.47: because you did not serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim with joy and gladness of heart for all the plenty.
28.48: “You shall serve your enemies whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sends against you, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in need of all. And he shall put a yoke of iron on your neck until he has destroyed you.
28.49: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 brings a nation against you from afar, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flies, a nation whose language you shall not understand,
28.50: a fierce-looking nation, which shows no regard for the elderly nor show favor to the young,
28.51: and they shall eat the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your land, until you are destroyed. They leave you no grain, nor new wine, nor oil, nor the increase of your cattle or the offspring of your flocks, until they have destroyed you.
28.52: “And they shall besiege you at all your gates till your high and fenced walls, in which you are trusting, come down in all your land. And they shall besiege you at all your gates in all your land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has given you.
28.53: “And you shall eat the fruit of your own body, the flesh of your sons and your daughters whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has given you, in the siege and distress in which your enemies distress you.
28.54: “The man among you who is tender, and who is very delicate, his eye is evil against his brother, against the wife of his bosom, and against the rest of his children whom he leaves behind,
28.55: against giving any of them the flesh of his children that he eats, because it is all that has been left to him in the siege and distress with which your enemy distresses you in all your gates.
28.56: “The tender and the delicate woman among you, who have not tried to put the sole of her foot on the ground because of her delicateness and tenderness, her eye is evil against the husband of her bosom, and against her son, and against her daughter,
28.57: and against her seed which comes out from between her legs, and her children whom she bears, for she eats them in secret for lack of all, in the siege and distress with which your enemy distresses you in all your gates.
28.58: “If you do not guard to do all the Words of this Torah that are written in this Book, to revere this esteemed and awesome Name, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim,
28.59: then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall bring upon you and your descendants extraordinary plagues, great and lasting plagues, and grievous and lasting sicknesses.
28.60: “And He shall bring back on you all the diseases of Mitsrayim, of which you were afraid, and they shall cling to you,
28.61: also every sickness and every plague, which is not written in the Book of this Torah, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 brings upon you until you are destroyed.
28.62: “And you shall be left with few men, although you had become as numerous as the stars of the shamayim, because you did not obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
28.63: “And it shall be, that as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 rejoiced over you to do you good and increase you, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 rejoices over you to destroy you and lay you waste. And you shall be plucked from off the land which you go to possess.
28.64: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall scatter you among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other, and there you shall serve other mighty ones, which neither you nor your fathers have known, wood and stone.
28.65: “And among those nations you are to find no rest, nor have a resting place for the sole of your foot. But there 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall give you a trembling heart, and failing eyes, and sorrow of being.
28.66: “And your life shall be hanging in suspense before you, and you shall fear day and night, and not be certain of your life.
28.67: “In the morning you say, ‘Oh, that it were evening!’ And at evening you say, ‘Oh, that it were morning!’ because of the fear of your heart, with which you fear, and because of the sight which your eyes see.
28.68: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall bring you back to Mitsrayim in ships, by a way of which I said to you, ‘You are never to see it again.’ And there you shall be sold to your enemies as male and female slaves, but no one to buy.”

29.1: These are the words of the Covenant which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded Mosheh to make with the children of Yisra’ĕl in the land of Mo’aḇ, besides the Covenant which He made with them in Ḥorĕḇ.
29.2: And Mosheh called all Yisra’ĕl and said to them, “You yourselves saw all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 did before your eyes in the land of Mitsrayim, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land.
29.3: “Your eyes saw the great trials, the signs, and those great wonders.
29.4: “But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has not given you a heart to know and eyes to see and ears to hear, till this day.
29.5: “And I have led you forty years in the wilderness. Your garments have not worn out on you, and your sandals have not worn out on your feet.
29.6: “You ate no bread and drank no wine nor strong drink, so that you might know that I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
29.7: “And when you came to this place, Siḥon meleḵ of Ḥeshbon and Oḡ meleḵ of Bashan came out against us to battle, and we smote them,
29.8: and took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Re’uḇĕnites, and to the Gaḏites, and to half the tribe of Menashsheh.
29.9: “Therefore you shall guard the words of this Covenant, and do them, so that you prosper in all that you do.
29.10: “All of you are standing today before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim: your leaders, your tribes, your elders and your officers, all the men of Yisra’ĕl,
29.11: your little ones, your wives, and your sojourner who is in the midst of your camp, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water,
29.12: so that you should enter into Covenant with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and into His oath, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim makes with you today,
29.13: in order to establish you today as a people for Himself, and He Himself be your Elohim, as He has spoken to you, and as He has sworn to your fathers, to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya’aqoḇ.
29.14: “And not with you alone I am making this Covenant and this oath,
29.15: but with him who stands here with us today before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, as well as with him who is not here with us today.
29.16: “For you know how we dwelt in the land of Mitsrayim and how we passed through the nations which you passed through,
29.17: and you saw their abominations and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which were with them,
29.18: lest there should be among you a man or woman or clan or tribe, whose heart turns away today from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, to go and serve the mighty ones of these nations, lest there should be among you a root bearing bitterness or wormwood.
29.19: “And it shall be, when he hears the words of this curse, that he should baraḵ himself in his heart, saying, ‘I have peace though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart,’ in order to add drunkenness to thirst.
29.20: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 would not forgive him, but rather, the displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and His jealousy shall burn against that man, and every curse that is written in this Book shall settle on him, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall blot out his name from under the shamayim.
29.21: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall separate him for evil, out of all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, according to all the curses of the Covenant that are written in this Book of the Torah.
29.22: “And the generation to come of your children who rise up after you, and the foreigner who comes from a far land, shall say when they see the plagues of that land and the sicknesses which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has sent into it:
29.23: ‘All its land is sulphur, salt, and burning; it is not sown, nor does it bear, nor does any grass grow there, like the overthrow of Seḏom and Amorah, Aḏmah and Tseḇoyim, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 overthrew in His displeasure and His wrath.’
29.24: “And all nations shall say, ‘Why has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 done so to this land? What does the heat of this great displeasure mean?’
29.25: “And it shall be said, ‘Because they have forsaken the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of their fathers, which He made with them when He brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim.
29.26: ‘And they went and served other mighty ones and bowed themselves to them, mighty ones that they did not know and that He had not given to them,
29.27: therefore the displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 burned against this land, to bring on it every curse that is written in this Book.
29.28: ‘And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 uprooted them from their land in displeasure, and in wrath, and in great rage, and cast them into another land, as it is today.’
29.29: “The hidden belongs to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, but what is revealed belongs to us and to our children forever, to do all the Words of this Torah.

3.1: “Then we turned and went up the way to Bashan. And Oḡ meleḵ of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Eḏre’i.
3.2: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, ‘Do not fear him, for I have given him and all his people and his land into your hand. And you shall do to him as you did to Siḥon meleḵ of the Amorites, who dwelt at Ḥeshbon.’
3.3: “So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim also gave into our hands Oḡ meleḵ of Bashan, with all his people, and we smote him until he had no survivors remaining.
3.4: “And we captured all his cities at that time. There was not a city which we did not take from them: sixty cities, all the district of Argoḇ, the reign of Oḡ in Bashan.
3.5: “All these cities were fenced with high walls, gates and bars, besides a great many unwalled towns.
3.6: “And we put them under the ban, as we did to Siḥon meleḵ of Ḥeshbon, putting the men, the women, and the children of every city under the ban.
3.7: “But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as booty for ourselves.
3.8: “And at that time we took the land, from the hand of the two melaḵim of the Amorites, that was beyond the Yardĕn, from the wadi Arnon to Mount Ḥermon -
3.9: Tsiḏonians call Ḥermon, Siryon and the Amorites call it Senir -
3.10: all the cities of the plain, all Gil’aḏ, and all Bashan, as far as Salḵah and Eḏre’i, cities of the reign of Oḡ in Bashan.
3.11: “For only Oḡ meleḵ of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Repha’ites. See, his bedstead was an iron bedstead. Is it not in Rabbah of the children of Ammon? Nine ammah is its length and four ammah its width, according to the ammah of a man.
3.12: “And this land, which we possessed at that time, from Aro’ĕr, which is by the wadi Arnon, and half the mountains of Gil’aḏ and its cities, I gave to the Re’uḇĕnites and the Gaḏites.
3.13: “And the rest of Gil’aḏ, and all Bashan, the reign of Oḡ, I gave to half the tribe of Menashsheh - all the district of Argoḇ, with all Bashan, called the land of the Repha’ites.
3.14: “Ya’ir son of Menashsheh had taken all the district of Argoḇ, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Ma’aḵathites, and called them after his own name: ha’Bashan Ḥawoth Ya’ir, to this day.
3.16: “And to the Re’uḇĕnites and the Gaḏites I gave from Gil’aḏ as far as the wadi Arnon, the middle of the wadi as the border, as far as the wadi Yabboq, the border of the children of Ammon,
3.17: and the desert plain, with the Yardĕn as the border, from Kinnereth as far as the Sea of the Araḇah, the Salt Sea, below the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
3.18: “And I commanded you at that time, saying, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has given you this land to possess. All you sons of might, pass over armed before your brothers, the children of Yisra’ĕl.
3.19: ‘But let your wives and your little ones, and your livestock - I know that you have much livestock - stay in your cities which I have given you,
3.20: until 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has given rest to your brothers as to you, and they also possess the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving them beyond the Yardĕn. Then you shall return, each man to his possession which I have given you.’
3.21: “And I commanded Yahoshua at that time, saying, ‘Your eyes have seen all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has done to these two melaḵim. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 does the same to all the reigns which you are passing over.
3.22: ‘Do not fear them, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim Himself fights for you.’
3.23: “And I pleaded with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at that time, saying,
3.24: ‘O Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your strong hand, for who is a mighty one in the shamayim or on earth who does according to Your works and according to Your might?
3.25: ‘I pray, let me pass over and see the good land beyond the Yardĕn, this good hill country, and Leḇanon.’
3.26: “But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was enraged with me, for your sake, and would not listen to me, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, ‘Enough of that! Speak no more to Me about this matter.
3.27: ‘Go up to the top of Pisgah, and lift up your eyes westward, and northward, and southward, and eastward, and look with your eyes, for you do not pass over this Yardĕn.
3.28: ‘But command Yahoshua, and strengthen him and make him brave, for he shall pass over before this people and causes them to inherit the land which you see.’
3.29: “And we dwelt in the valley opposite Bĕyth Pe’or.

30.1: “And it shall be, when all these words come upon you, the beraḵah and the curse which I have put before you, and you shall bring them back to your heart among all the gentiles where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim drives you,
30.2: and shall turn back to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim and obey His voice, according to all that I command you today, with all your heart and with all your being, you and your children,
30.3: then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall turn back your captivity, and shall have compassion on you, and He shall turn back and gather you from all the peoples where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has scattered you.
30.4: “If any of you are driven out to the farthest parts under the shamayim, from there 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim gathers you, and from there He takes you.
30.5: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall bring you to the land which your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it. And He shall do good to you, and increase you more than your fathers.
30.6: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall circumcise your heart and the heart of your seed, to love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim with all your heart and with all your being, so that you might live,
30.7: and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall put all these curses on your enemies and on those who hate you, who persecuted you.
30.8: “And you shall turn back and obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and do all His Commands which I command you today.
30.9: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall make you have excess in all the work of your hand, in the fruit of your body, and in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your ground for good. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 turns back to rejoice over you for good as He rejoiced over your fathers,
30.10: if you obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, to guard His Commands and His Laws which are written in this Book of the Torah, if you turn back to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim with all your heart and with all your being.
30.11: “For this Command which I am commanding you today, it is not too hard for you, nor is it far off.
30.12: “It is not in the shamayim, to say, ‘Who shall ascend into the shamayim for us, and bring it to us, and cause us to hear it, so that we do it?’
30.13: “Nor is it beyond the sea, to say, ‘Who shall go over the sea for us, and bring it to us, and cause us to hear it, so that we do it?’
30.14: “For the Word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart - to do it.
30.15: “See, I have put before you today ḥai and good, and death and evil,
30.16: in that I am commanding you today to love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, to walk in His Ways, and to guard His Commands, and His Laws, and His Right-Rulings. And you shall live and increase, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall baraḵ you in the land which you go to possess.
30.17: “But if your heart turns away, and you do not obey, and shall be drawn away, and shall bow down to other mighty ones and serve them,
30.18: “I have declared to you today that you shall certainly perish, you shall not prolong your days in the land which you are passing over the Yardĕn to enter and possess.
30.19: “I have called the shamayim and the earth as witnesses today against you: I have put before you ḥai and death, the beraḵah and the curse. Therefore you shall choose ḥai, so that you live, both you and your seed,
30.20: to love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, to obey His voice, and to cling to Him - for He is your ḥai and the length of your days - to dwell in the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 swore to your fathers, to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya’aqoḇ, to give them.”

31.1: And Mosheh went and spoke these words to all Yisra’ĕl,
31.2: and he said to them, “I am one hundred and twenty years old today. I am no longer able to go out and come in. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has said to me, ‘You do not pass over this Yardĕn.’
31.3: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim Himself is passing over before you. He shall destroy these nations from before you and you possess them. Yahoshua himself is passing over before you, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spoken.
31.4: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall do to them as He did to Siḥon and to Oḡ, the melaḵim of the Amorites and their land, when He destroyed them.
31.5: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall give them over to you, and you shall do to them according to all the Command which I have commanded you.
31.6: “Be strong and courageous, do not fear nor be afraid of them. For it is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim who is going with you. He does not fail you nor forsake you.”
31.7: And Mosheh called Yahoshua and said to him before the eyes of all Yisra’ĕl, “Be strong and courageous, for you are going with this people to the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has sworn to their fathers to give them, and you are to let them inherit it.
31.8: “And it is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who is going before you, He Himself is with you. He does not fail you nor forsake you. Do not fear nor be discouraged.”
31.9: And Mosheh wrote this Torah and gave it to the kohenim, the sons of Lĕwi, who bore the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and to all the elders of Yisra’ĕl.
31.10: And Mosheh commanded them, saying, “At the end of seven years, at the Appointed Time, the year of release, at the Festival of Sukkoth,
31.11: when all Yisra’ĕl comes to appear before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim in the place which He chooses, read this Torah before all Yisra’ĕl in their hearing.
31.12: “Assemble the people, the men and the women and the little ones, and your sojourner who is within your gates, so that they hear, and so that they learn to revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim and guard to do all the Words of this Torah.
31.13: “And their children, who have not known it, should hear and learn to revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim as long as you live in the land you are passing over the Yardĕn to possess.”
31.14: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Mosheh, “See, the days have drawn near for you to die. Call Yahoshua, and present yourselves in the Tent of Appointment, so that I command him.” And Mosheh and Yahoshua went and presented themselves in the Tent of Appointment.
31.15: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared at the Tent in a column of a cloud, and the column of a cloud stood above the door of the Tent.
31.16: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Mosheh, “See, you are about to sleep with your fathers. And this people shall rise and whore after the mighty ones of the strangers of the land into the midst of which they shall enter, and forsake Me and break My Covenant which I have made with them.
31.17: “Then My displeasure shall burn against them in that day, and I shall forsake them and hide My face from them, and they shall be consumed. And many evils and distresses shall come upon them, and it shall be said in that day, ‘Is it not because our Elohim is not in our midst that these evils have come upon us?’
31.18: “And I shall certainly hide My face in that day, because of all the evil which they have done, for they shall turn to other mighty ones.
31.19: “And now write down this song for yourselves, and teach it to the children of Yisra’ĕl. Put it in their mouths, so that this song is to Me for a witness against the children of Yisra’ĕl.
31.20: “And I shall bring them to the land flowing with milk and honey, of which I swore to their fathers, and they shall eat and be satisfied and be fat, then they shall turn to other mighty ones, and they shall serve them, and scorn Me and break My Covenant.
31.21: “And it shall be, when many evils and distresses come upon them, that this song shall answer before them as a witness. For it is not to be forgotten in the mouths of their seed, for I know their thoughts which they are forming today, even before I bring them to the land of which I swore to give them.”
31.22: And Mosheh wrote this song the same day, and taught it to the children of Yisra’ĕl.
31.23: And He commanded Yahoshua son of Nun, and said, “Be strong and courageous, for you are to bring the children of Yisra’ĕl into the land of which I swore to them, and I Myself am with you.”
31.24: And it came to be, when Mosheh had completed writing the Words of this Torah in a Book, until their completion,
31.25: that Mosheh commanded the Lĕwites, who bore the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying,
31.26: “Take this Book of the Torah, and you shall place it beside the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and it shall be there as a witness against you,
31.27: for I myself know your rebellion and your stiff neck. See, while I am still alive with you today, you have been rebellious against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, then how much more after my death?
31.28: “Assemble unto me all the elders of your tribes, and your officers, so that I speak these words in their hearing and call the shamayim and the earth to witness against them.
31.29: “For I know that after my death you shall do very corruptly and turn aside from the Way which I have commanded you. And evil shall come to you in the latter days, because you do what is evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to provoke Him through the work of your hands.”
31.30: So Mosheh spoke in the hearing of all the assembly of Yisra’ĕl the words of this song till their completion:

32.2:
“Let my instruction fall as rain, 
My speech drop down as dew, 
As fine rain on the tender plants, 
And as showers on the grass.
32.3:
“For I proclaim the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
Ascribe greatness to our Elohim.
32.4:
“The Rock! His work is perfect, 
For all His Ways are right-ruling, 
An Ĕl of truth and without unrighteousness, 
Righteous and straight is He.
32.5:
“A twisted and wicked generation has corrupted itself, 
Their blemish, not His children.
32.6:
“Do you do this to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
O foolish and unwise people? 
Is He not your Father, who bought you, 
Who created you and established you?
32.7:
“Remember the days of old, 
Consider the years of many generations. 
Ask your father and let him show you, 
Your elders, and let them say to you:
32.8:
“When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, 
When He separated the sons of Aḏam, 
He established the boundaries of the peoples 
According to the number of the children of Yisra’ĕl.
32.9:
“For the portion of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is His people, 
Ya’aqoḇ His allotted inheritance.
32.10:
“He found him in a wilderness, 
And in a wasted, howling desert. 
He encompassed him, He made him understand, 
He watched over him as the apple of His eye.
32.11:
“As an eagle stirs up its nest, 
Flutters over its young, 
Spreading out its wings, taking them up, 
Bearing them on its wings.
32.12:
“𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 alone led him, 
And there was no strange mighty one with him.
32.13:
“He made him ride in the heights of the earth, 
And he ate the fruit of the fields, 
And He made him to draw honey from the rock, 
And oil from the flinty rock,
32.14:
“Curds from the cattle, 
And milk of the flock, 
With fatness of lambs, 
And rams of the breed of Bashan, 
And goats, with the choicest wheat; 
And you drank wine, the blood of grapes.
32.16:
“They moved Him to jealousy with the foreign, 
With abominations they provoked Him.
32.17:
“They slaughtered to demons - not Eloah -
Mighty ones they did not know, 
New ones who came lately, 
Which your fathers did not reverence.
32.18:
“You neglected the Rock who brought you forth, 
And forgot the Ĕl who fathered you.
32.19:
“And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saw, and despised, 
Because of the provocation of His sons and His daughters.
32.20:
“And He said, ‘Let Me hide My face from them, 
Let Me see what their end is, 
For they are a perverse generation, 
Children in whom there is no trusting.
32.21:
“They made Me jealous by what is not Ĕl. 
They provoked Me with their worthlessness. 
But I make them jealous by those who are no people, 
I provoke them with a foolish nation.
32.22:
“For a fire was kindled in My wrath 
And burns to the bottom of She’ol, 
And consumes the earth and its increase, 
And lights on fire the foundations of mountains.
32.23:
“I gather evils upon them, 
I use up My arrows upon them -
32.24:
“Wasted by scarcity of food, 
And consumed by heat and bitter destruction, 
And the teeth of beasts I send upon them, 
With the poison of serpents of the dust.
32.25:
“The sword bereaves from the outside, 
And fear from within, 
Both young man and maiden, 
Nursing child with the man of grey hairs.
32.26:
“I said, ‘I should blow them away, 
I should make the remembrance of them 
To cease from among men,
32.27:
“If I did not fear the enemy’s taunt, 
Lest their adversaries misunderstand, 
Lest they say, “Our hand is high, 
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has not done all this.” ’
32.28:
“For they are a nation lost to counsel, 
And there is no understanding in them.
32.29:
“If they were wise, 
They would understand this, 
They would consider their latter end!
32.30:
“How would one chase a thousand, 
And two put ten thousand to flight, 
Unless their Rock had sold them, 
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had given them up?
32.31:
“For their rock is not like our Rock -
Even our enemies are judges.
32.32:
“Their vine is of the vine of Seḏom 
And of the fields of Amorah; 
Their grapes are grapes of gall, 
Their clusters are bitter.
32.33:
“Their wine is the poison of serpents, 
And the fierce venom of cobras.
32.34:
‘Is it not stored up with Me, 
Sealed up among My treasures?
32.35:
‘Vengeance is Mine, and repayment, 
At the time their foot slips; 
For near is the day of their calamity, 
And the preparations are hastening to them.’
32.36:
“For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 rightly rules His people 
And has compassion on His servants, 
When He sees that their power is gone, 
And there is no one remaining, 
Shut up or at large.
32.37:
“And He shall say, ‘Where are their mighty ones, 
The rock in whom they sought refuge?
32.38:
‘Who ate the fat of their slaughterings, 
And drank the wine of their drink offering? 
Let them arise and help you, 
Let it be a hiding-place for you!
32.39:
‘See now that I, I am He, 
And there is no Elohim besides Me. 
I put to death and I make alive. 
I have wounded, and I heal. 
And from My hand no one delivers!
32.40:
‘For I lift My hand to the shamayim, 
And shall say: As I live forever,
32.41:
‘If I have sharpened My flashing sword, 
And My hand takes hold on judgment, 
I shall return vengeance to My enemies, 
And repay those who hate Me.
32.42:
‘I make My arrows drunk with blood, 
And My sword devours flesh, 
With the blood of the slain and the captives, 
From the long-haired enemy chiefs.’
32.43:
“O nations, acclaim His people! 
For He avenges the blood of His servants, 
And returns vengeance to His adversaries, 
And shall pardon His land, His people.”
32.44: Then Mosheh came, with Yahoshua son of Nun, and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people.
32.45: And when Mosheh ended speaking all these words to all Yisra’ĕl,
32.46: he said to them, “Lay your heart on all the words with which I warn you today, so that you command your children to guard to do all the Words of this Torah.
32.47: “For it is not a worthless Word for you, because it is your ḥai, and by this Word you prolong your days on the land which you pass over the Yardĕn to possess.”
32.48: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh that same day, saying,
32.49: “Go up this mountain of the Aḇarim, Mount Neḇo, which is in the land of Mo’aḇ, which is opposite Yeriḥo, and look at the land of Kena’an, which I give to the children of Yisra’ĕl as a possession,
32.50: and die on the mountain which you ascend, and be gathered to your people, as Aharon your brother died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people,
32.51: because you trespassed against Me in the midst of the children of Yisra’ĕl at the waters of Meriḇah Qaḏĕsh, in the Wilderness of Tsin, because you did not qadosh Me in the midst of the children of Yisra’ĕl.
32.52: “For you are to look at the land before you, but not enter there, into the land which I am giving to the children of Yisra’ĕl.”

33.1: And this is the beraḵah with which Mosheh the man of Elohim baraḵ the children of Yisra’ĕl before his death.
33.2: And he said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came from Sinai, and rose from Sĕ’ir for them. He shone forth from Mount Paran, and came with ten thousands of qodeshim - at His right hand a law of fire for them.
33.3: Indeed, He loves the peoples, all His qodeshim are in Your hand. And they, they sat down at Your feet, receiving Your Words.
33.4: Mosheh commanded us a Torah, an inheritance of the assembly of Ya’aqoḇ.
33.5: And He was Meleḵ in Yeshurun, when the heads of the people were gathered, the tribes of Yisra’ĕl
33.6: “Let Re’uḇĕn live, and not die, and let his men be numbered.”
33.7: And this of Yahuḏah, and he said, “Hear, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the voice of Yahuḏah, and bring him to his people. His hands shall fight for him, and You be a help against his enemies.”
33.8: And of Lĕwi he said, “Your Tummim and Your Urim belong to Your kind one, whom You tried at Massah, with whom You contended at the waters of Meriḇah,
33.9: who said of his father and mother, ‘I have not seen them.’ And he did not acknowledge his brothers, or know his own children, for they have guarded Your Word and watched over Your Covenant.
33.10: “They teach Your Right-Rulings to Ya’aqoḇ, and Your Torah to Yisra’ĕl. They put incense before You, and a complete burnt offering on Your altar.
33.11: “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 baraḵ his strength, and accept the work of his hands. Strike through the loins of those who rise against him, and of those who hate him, that they rise no more.”
33.12: Of Binyamin he said, “Let the beloved of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 dwell in safety by Him, shielding him all the day, as he dwells between His shoulders.”
33.13: And of Yosĕph he said, “Meḇoreḵeth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is his land, with the choicest from the shamayim, with the dew, and the deep lying beneath,
33.14: with the choice fruits of the sun, with the choice yield of the months,
33.15: with the finest of the ancient mountains, with the choicest of the everlasting hills,
33.16: with the choicest of the earth and all that fills it, and the good pleasure of Him who dwelt in the bush. Let it come on the head of Yosĕph, and on the crown of the head of him who was separate from his brothers.
33.17: “His splendor is like a first-born bull, and his horns are like the horns of the wild ox. With them he pushes the peoples to the ends of the earth. Andthey are the ten thousands of Ephrayim, and they are the thousands of Menashsheh.”
33.18: And of Zeḇulun he said, “Rejoice. O Zeḇulun, in your going out, and Yissasḵar in your tents!
33.19: “They call peoples to the mountain, there they bring offerings of righteousness, for they draw from the riches of the seas, and treasures hidden in the sand.”
33.20: And of Gaḏ he said. “Baruḵ is he who enlarges Gaḏ. He dwells as a lion, and shall tear off the arm, also the crown.
33.21: “And he chose the best for himself, for there the portion of the lawgiver was hidden. And he came with the heads of the people. The righteousness of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 he did, and His Right-Rulings with Yisra’ĕl.”
33.22: And of Dan he said, “Dan is a lion’s cub, that leaps from Bashan.”
33.23: And of Naphtali he said, “O Naphtali, satisfied with pleasure, and filled with the beraḵah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, possess the west and the south.”
33.24: And of Ashĕr he said, “Ashĕr is most baruḵ of sons. Let him be accepted by his brothers, and dip his foot in oil.
33.25: “Your sandals are iron and bronze, and your strength as your days.
33.26: “O Yeshurun, there is no one like Ĕl, riding the shamayim to help you, and on the clouds, in His excellency.
33.27: “The Elohim of old is a refuge, and beneath are everlasting arms. And He drives out the enemy from before you and says, ‘Destroy!’
33.28: ‘Thus Yisra’ĕl dwells in safety, the fountain of Ya’aqoḇ alone, in a land of grain and new wine. His shamayim also drop down dew.
33.29: “Ashrĕ are you, O Yisra’ĕl! Who is like you? A people saved by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the shield of your help, and He who is the sword of your excellency! And your enemies are subdued for you, and you tread down their high places.”

34.1: And Mosheh went up from the desert plains of Mo’aḇ to Mount Neḇo, to the top of Pisgah, which is opposite Yeriḥo. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 showed him all the land of Gil’aḏ as far as Dan.
34.2: and all Naphtali and the land of Ephrayim and Menashsheh, all the land of Yahuḏah as far as the Western Sea,
34.3: and the Negeḇ, and the plain of the Valley of Yeriḥo, the city of palm trees, as far as Tso’ar.
34.4: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to him, “This is the land of which I swore to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya’aqoḇ, saying, ‘To your seed I give it.’ I have let you look at it with your eyes, but you do not pass over there.”
34.5: And Mosheh the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 died there in the land of Mo’aḇ, according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
34.6: And He buried him in a valley in the land of Mo’aḇ, opposite Bĕyth Pe’or, and no one knows his burial place to this day.
34.7: And Mosheh was one hundred and twenty years old when he died. His eyes were not dim nor his freshness gone.
34.8: And the children of Yisra’ĕl wept for Mosheh in the desert plains of Mo’aḇ thirty days. And the days of weeping and mourning for Mosheh were completed.
34.9: And Yahoshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, for Mosheh had laid his hands on him. And the children of Yisra’ĕl listened to him, and did as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded Mosheh.
34.10: And since then no naḇi has arisen in Yisra’ĕl like Mosheh, whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 knew face to face,
34.11: for all the signs and wonders which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent him to do in the land of Mitsrayim, before Pharaoh, and before all his servants, and in all his land,
34.12: and for all that strong hand and all the great fearsome deeds which Mosheh did before the eyes of all Yisra’ĕl.

4.1: “And now, O Yisra’ĕl, listen to the Laws and the Right-Rulings which I am teaching you to do, so that you live, and shall go in and possess the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of your fathers is giving you.
4.2: “Do not add to the Word which I command you, and do not take away from it, so as to guard the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim which I am commanding you.
4.3: “Your eyes have seen what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 did at Ba’al Pe’or, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has destroyed from your midst all the men who followed Ba’al Pe’or.
4.4: “But you who are clinging to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim are alive today, every one of you.
4.5: “See, I have taught you Laws and Right-Rulings, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim commanded me, to do thus in the land which you go to possess.
4.6: “And you shall guard and do them, for this is your wisdom and your understanding before the eyes of the peoples who hear all these Laws, and they shall say, ‘Only a wise and understanding people is this great nation!’
4.7: “For what great nation is there which has Elohim so near to it, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim is to us, whenever we call on Him?
4.8: “And what great nation is there that has such Laws and righteous Right-Rulings like all this Torah which I put before you this day?
4.9: “Only, guard yourself, and guard your ḥai diligently, lest you forget the Words your eyes have seen, and lest they turn aside from your heart all the days of your life. And you shall make them known to your children and your grandchildren.
4.10: “The day when you stood before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim in Ḥorĕḇ, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, ‘Assemble the people to Me and I make them hear My Words, so that they learn to revere Me all the days they live on the earth and teach their children.’
4.11: “And you came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, and the mountain burned with fire to the heart of the shamayim - darkness and cloud, dense cloud.
4.12: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to you out of the midst of the fire. You heard a voice of words, but saw no form, you only heard a voice.
4.13: “And He made known to you His Covenant which He commanded you to do, the Ten Words, and He wrote them on two tablets of stone.
4.14: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded me at that time to teach you Laws and Right-Rulings, for you to do them in the land which you pass over to possess.
4.15: “Therefore, diligently guard yourselves, for you saw no form when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to you at Ḥorĕḇ out of the midst of the fire,
4.16: lest you should do corruptly and shall make for yourselves a carved image in the form of any figure - the likeness of male or female,
4.17: the likeness of any beast that is on the earth or the likeness of any winged bird that flies in the shamayim,
4.18: the likeness of any creature that creeps on the ground or the likeness of any fish that is in the water under the earth;
4.19: and lest you lift up your eyes to the shamayim, and shall see the sun, and the moon, and the stars - all the host of the shamayim - and you be drawn away into bowing down to them and serving them, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has allotted to all the peoples under all the shamayim.
4.20: “But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Mitsrayim, to be His people, an inheritance, as it is today.
4.21: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was enraged with me because of your words, and swore that I would not pass over the Yardĕn, and that I would not enter the good land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you as an inheritance.
4.22: “For I am to die in this land, I am not passing over the Yardĕn, but you are passing over, and shall possess that good land.
4.23: “Guard yourselves, lest you forget the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim which He made with you, and shall make for yourselves a carved image in any likeness 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has commanded you.
4.24: “For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is a consuming fire, a jealous Ĕl.
4.25: “When you bring forth children and grandchildren, and shall grow old in the land, and shall do corruptly and make a carved image in any likeness, and shall do what is evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim to provoke Him,
4.26: “I shall call the shamayim and earth to witness against you on that day, that you soon completely perish from the land which you pass over the Yardĕn to possess - you do not prolong your days in it but are completely destroyed.
4.27: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall scatter you among the peoples, and you shall be left few in number among the gentiles where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 drives you.
4.28: “And there you shall serve mighty ones, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, which neither see nor hear nor eat nor smell.
4.29: “But from there you shall seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and shall find, when you search for Him with all your heart and with all your being.
4.30: “In your distress, when all these words shall come upon you in the latter days, then you shall return to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim and shall obey His voice.
4.31: “For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is a compassionate Ĕl, He does not forsake you, nor destroy you, nor forget the Covenant of your fathers which He swore to them.
4.32: “For ask now of the days that are past, which were before you, since the day that Elohim created man on the earth, and ask from one end of the shamayim to the other end of the shamayim, whether there has been a Word as great as this, or has been heard like it.
4.33: “Has a people heard the voice of Elohim speaking out of the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and live?
4.34: “Or has Elohim tried to go and take for Himself a nation from the midst of a nation by trials, and by signs, and by wonders, and by battle, and by a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and by great fearsome deeds, according to all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim did for you in Mitsrayim before your eyes?
4.35: “You have been shown it, to know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Himself is Elohim; there is no one beside Him.
4.36: “From the shamayim He let you hear His voice, to instruct you, and on earth He showed you His great fire, and you heard His words out of the midst of the fire.
4.37: “And because He loved your fathers, therefore He chose their seed after them, and brought you out of Mitsrayim with His Presence, with His great power,
4.38: to drive out from before you nations greater and stronger than you, to bring you in, to give you their land as an inheritance, as it is today.
4.39: “And you shall know today, and shall recall to your heart that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Himself is Elohim in the shamayim above and on the earth beneath; there is none else.
4.40: “And you shall guard His Laws and His Commands which I command you today, so that it is well with you and with your children after you, and so that you prolong your days on the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you for all time.”
4.41: Then Mosheh separated three cities beyond the Yardĕn, toward the rising of the sun,
4.42: for him who killed someone to flee there, he who kills his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him in time past, and might flee to one of these cities and live:
4.43: Betser in the wilderness in the level land for the Re’uḇĕnites, and Ramoth in Gil’aḏ for the Gaḏites, and Golan in Bashan for the Menashshites.
4.44: And this is the Torah which Mosheh put before the children of Yisra’ĕl.
4.45: These are the Witnesses, and the Laws, and the Right-Rulings which Mosheh spoke to the children of Yisra’ĕl after they came out of Mitsrayim,
4.46: beyond the Yardĕn, in the valley opposite Bĕyth Pe’or, in the land of Siḥon meleḵ of the Amorites, who dwelt at Ḥeshbon, whom Mosheh and the children of Yisra’ĕl had smitten after they came out of Mitsrayim.
4.47: And they took possession of his land and the land of Oḡ meleḵ of Bashan, two melaḵim of the Amorites, who were beyond the Yardĕn, toward the rising of the sun,
4.48: from Aro’ĕr, which is on the bank of the wadi Arnon, even to Mount Siyon, which is Ḥermon,
4.49: and all the desert plain beyond the Yardĕn as far as the Sea of the Araḇah, below the slopes of Pisgah.

5.1: And Mosheh called all Yisra’ĕl, and said to them, “Hear, O Yisra’ĕl, the Laws and Right-Rulings which I speak in your hearing today. And you shall learn them, and guard to do them.
5.2: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim made a Covenant with us in Ḥorĕḇ.
5.3: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 did not make this Covenant with our fathers, but with us, those who are here today, all of us who are alive.
5.4: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke with you face to face on the mountain from the midst of the fire.
5.5: “I stood between 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and you at that time, to declare to you the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 - for you were afraid because of the fire, and you did not go up the mountain - saying:
5.6: ‘I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, out of the house of bondage.
5.7: ‘You have no other mighty ones against My face.
5.8: ‘You do not make for yourself a carved image, any likeness of which is in the shamayim above, or which is in the earth beneath, or which is in the waters under the earth,
5.9: you do not bow down to them nor serve them. For I, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, am a jealous Ĕl, visiting the wickedness of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me,
5.10: but showing kindness to thousands, to those who love Me and guard My Commands.
5.11: ‘You do not bring the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim to naught, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 does not leave him unpunished who brings His Name to naught.
5.12: ‘Guard the Shabbath day, to qadosh it, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim commanded you.
5.13: ‘Six days you labor, and shall do all your work,
5.14: but the seventh day is a Shabbath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim. You do not do any work - you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your ox, nor your donkey, nor any of your cattle, nor your stranger who is within your gates, so that your male servant and your female servant rest as you do.
5.15: ‘And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Mitsrayim, and that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim brought you out from there by a strong hand and by an outstretched arm. Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim commanded you to perform the Shabbath day.
5.16: ‘Respect your father and your mother, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has commanded you, so that your days are prolonged, and so that it is well with you on the land which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is giving you.
5.20: ‘You do not bear false witness against your neighbor.
5.21: ‘You do not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor do you desire your neighbor’s house, his field, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, his ox, nor his donkey, or whatever belongs to your neighbor.’
5.22: “These Words 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to all your assembly, in the mountain from the midst of the fire, of the cloud, and of the dense cloud, with a loud voice, and He added no more. And He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.
5.23: “And it came to be, when you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, that you came near to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders,
5.24: and said, ‘See, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim has shown us His esteem and His greatness, and we have heard His voice from the midst of the fire. Today we have seen that Elohim speaks with man - and he lives!
5.25: ‘And now why should we die? For this great fire is consuming us. If we hear the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim any more, then we shall die.
5.26: ‘For who is there of all flesh who has heard the voice of the living Elohim speaking from the midst of the fire, as we have, and lived?
5.27: ‘You go near and hear all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim says, and speak to us all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim says to you, and we shall hear and do it.’
5.28: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 heard the voice of your words when you spoke to me, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, ‘I have heard the voice of the words of this people which they have spoken to you. They have done well in all that they have spoken.
5.29: ‘Oh, that they had such a heart in them, to revere Me and to guard all My Commands always, so that it might be well with them and with their children forever!
5.30: ‘Go, say to them, “Return to your tents.”
5.31: ‘But you, stand here by Me, and let Me speak to you all the Commands, and the Laws, and the Right-Rulings which you are to teach them. And they shall do them in the land which I am giving them to possess.’
5.32: “And you shall guard to do as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has commanded you - do not turn aside, to the right or to the left.
5.33: “Walk in all the Way which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has commanded you, so that you live and it be well with you. And you shall prolong your days in the land which you possess.

6.1: “And this is the Command, the Laws and Right-Rulings which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has commanded, to teach you to do in the land which you are passing over to possess,
6.2: so that you revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, to guard all His Laws and His Commands which I command you, you and your son and your grandson, all the days of your life, and that your days be prolonged.
6.3: “And you shall hear, O Yisra’ĕl, and shall guard to do, that it might be well with you, and that you increase greatly as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of your fathers has spoken to you, a land flowing with milk and honey.
6.4: “Hear, O Yisra’ĕl: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is one!
6.5: “And you shall love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim with all your heart, and with all your being, and with all your might.
6.6: “And these Words which I am commanding you today shall be in your heart,
6.7: and you shall impress them upon your children, and shall speak of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up,
6.8: and shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes.
6.9: “And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
6.10: “And it shall be, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim brings you into the land of which He swore to your fathers, to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya’aqoḇ, to give you great and good cities which you did not build,
6.11: and houses filled with all kinds of goods, which you did not fill, and wells dug which you did not dig, vineyards and olive trees which you did not plant, and you shall eat and be satisfied -
6.12: be on guard, lest you forget 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, from the house of bondage.
6.13: “Revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim and serve Him, and swear by His Name.
6.14: “Do not go after other mighty ones, the mighty ones of the peoples who are all around you,
6.15: for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is a jealous Ĕl in your midst, lest the displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim burn against you, then He shall destroy you from the face of the earth.
6.16: “Do not try 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim as you tried Him in Massah.
6.17: “Diligently guard the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and His Witnesses, and His Laws which He has commanded you.
6.18: “And you shall do what is right and good in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that it might be well with you, and you shall go in and possess the good land of which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 swore to your fathers,
6.19: to drive out all your enemies from before you, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spoken.
6.20: “When your son asks you in time to come, saying, ‘What is the meaning of the Witnesses, and the Laws, and the Right-Rulings which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim has commanded you?’
6.21: then you shall say to your son, ‘We were slaves of Pharaoh in Mitsrayim, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 brought us out of Mitsrayim with a strong hand,
6.22: and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent signs and wonders, great and grievous, upon Mitsrayim, upon Pharaoh, and upon all his household, before our eyes.
6.23: ‘And He brought us out from there, to bring us in, to give us the land of which He swore to our fathers.
6.24: ‘And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded us to do all these Laws, to revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, for our good always, to keep us alive, as it is today.
6.25: ‘And it is righteousness for us when we guard to do all this Command before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, as He has commanded us.’

7.1: “When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim brings you into the land which you go to possess, He shall also clear away many nations before you: the Ḥittites and the Girgashites and the Amorites and the Kena’anites and the Perizzites and the Ḥiwwites and the Yeḇusites, seven nations greater and mightier than you.
7.2: “And when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim gives them over to you, you shall smite them and put them under the ban, completely. Make no covenant with them, and show them no favor.
7.3: “And do not intermarry with them - you do not give your daughter to his son, and you do not take his daughter for your son,
7.4: for he turns your sons away from following Me, to serve other mighty ones. Then the displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall burn against you and promptly destroy you.
7.5: “But this is what you do to them: Break down their altars, and destroy their pillars, and cut down their Ashĕrim, and burn their carved images with fire.
7.6: “For you are a qodesh people to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has chosen you to be a people for Himself, a treasured possession above all the peoples on the face of the earth.
7.7: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 did not place His love on you nor choose you because you were more numerous than any other people, for you were the least of all peoples,
7.8: but because of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 loving you, and because of Him guarding the oath which He swore to your fathers, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has brought you out with a strong hand, and redeemed you from the house of bondage, from the hand of Pharaoh meleḵ of Mitsrayim.
7.9: “And you shall know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, He is Elohim, the trustworthy Ĕl guarding Covenant and kindness for a thousand generations with those who love Him, and those who guard His Commands,
7.10: but repaying those who hate Him to their face, to destroy them. He does not delay with him who hates Him, He repays him to his face.
7.11: “And you shall guard the Command, and the Laws, and the Right-Rulings which I command you today, to do them.
7.12: “And it shall be, because you hear these Right-Rulings, and shall guard and do them, that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall guard with you the Covenant and the kindness which He swore to your fathers,
7.13: and shall love you and baraḵ you and increase you, and shall baraḵ the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your land, your grain and your new wine and your oil, the increase of your cattle and the offspring of your flock, in the land of which He swore to your fathers to give you.
7.14: “Baruḵ are you above all peoples - there is not going to be a barren man or a barren woman among you or among your livestock.
7.15: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall turn away from you all sickness and put on you none of the evil diseases of Mitsrayim which you have known, but He shall put them on all those who hate you.
7.16: “And you shall consume all the peoples whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is delivering over to you - your eye shall not pardon them. And do not serve their mighty ones, for that is a snare to you.
7.17: “When you say in your heart, ‘These nations are greater than I, I am unable to drive them out,’
7.18: do not be afraid of them. Remember well what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim did to Pharaoh and to all Mitsrayim,
7.19: the great trials which your eyes saw, and the signs and the wonders, the strong hand and the outstretched arm, by which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim brought you out. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim does so to all the peoples of whose presence you are afraid.
7.20: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim also sends the hornet among them until those who are left, who hide themselves from you, are destroyed.
7.21: “Do not be afraid of them, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, the great and awesome Ĕl, is in your midst.
7.22: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall drive out those nations before you, little by little. You are not allowed to destroy them at once, lest the beasts of the field become too numerous for you.
7.23: “But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim shall deliver them over to you and destroy them with a great destruction until they are consumed.
7.24: “And He shall give their melaḵim into your hand, and you shall destroy their name from under the shamayim. No one is going to be able to stand against you until you have destroyed them.
7.25: “The carved images of their mighty ones you are to burn with fire. Do not covet the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it for yourselves, lest you be snared by it, for it is an abomination to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
7.26: “And do not bring an abomination into your house, lest you be accursed like it. Utterly loathe it and utterly hate it, for it is accursed.

8.1: “Guard to do every Command which I command you today, that you might live, and shall increase, and go in, and shall possess the land of which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 swore to your fathers.
8.2: “And you shall remember that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim led you all the way these forty years in the wilderness, to humble you, prove you, to know what is in your heart, whether you guard His Commands or not.
8.3: “And He humbled you, and let you suffer hunger, and fed you with manna which you did not know nor did your fathers know, to make you know that man does not live by bread alone, but by all that comes from the mouth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
8.4: “Your garments did not wear out on you, nor did your foot swell these forty years.
8.5: “Thus you shall know in your heart that as a man disciplines his son, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim disciplines you,
8.6: therefore you shall guard the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, to walk in His Ways and to revere Him.
8.7: “For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is bringing you into a good land, a land of streams of water, of fountains and springs, that flow out of valleys and hills,
8.8: a land of wheat and barley, of vines and fig trees and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey,
8.9: a land in which you eat bread without scarcity, in which you do not lack at all, a land whose stones are iron and out of whose hills you dig copper.
8.10: “And you shall eat and be satisfied, and shall baraḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim for the good land which He has given you.
8.11: “Be on guard, lest you forget 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim by not guarding His Commands, and His Right-Rulings, and His Laws which I command you today,
8.12: lest you eat and shall be satisfied, and build lovely houses and shall dwell in them,
8.13: and your herds and your flocks increase, and your silver and your gold are increased, and all that you have is increased,
8.14: that your heart then becomes lifted up, and you forget 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, from the house of bondage,
8.15: who led you through that great and awesome wilderness - fiery serpents and scorpions and thirst - where there was no water, who brought water for you out of the flinty rock,
8.16: who fed you in the wilderness with manna, which your fathers did not know, in order to humble you and to try you, to do you good in the end,
8.17: you then shall say in your heart, ‘My power and the strength of my hand have made for me this wealth!’
8.18: “But you shall remember 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, for it is He who gives you power to get wealth, in order to establish His Covenant which He swore to your fathers, as it is today.
8.19: “And it shall be, if you by any means forget 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and follow other mighty ones, and serve them and bow yourself to them, I have warned you this day that you shall certainly perish.
8.20: “Like the nations which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is destroying before you, so you are to perish, because you did not obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.

9.1: “Hear, O Yisra’ĕl: You are passing over the Yardĕn today, to go in to dispossess nations greater and stronger than yourself, cities great and walled up to the shamayim,
9.2: a people great and tall, the descendants of the Anaqim, whom you know, and of whom you heard it said, ‘Who stands before the descendants of Anaq?’
9.3: “And you shall know today that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is He who is passing over before you as a consuming fire - He destroys them and subdues them before you. So you shall dispossess them and destroy them quickly, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has said to you.
9.4: “Do not think in your heart, after 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has driven them out before you, saying, ‘Because of my righteousness 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has brought me in to possess this land.’ But it is because of the wickedness of these nations that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is driving them out from before you.
9.5: “It is not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart that you go in to possess their land, but because of the wickedness of these nations that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim drives them out from before you, in order to establish the word which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 swore to your fathers, to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya’aqoḇ.
9.6: “And you shall know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is not giving you this good land to possess because of your righteousness, for you are a stiff-necked people.
9.7: “Remember, do not forget how you provoked to wrath 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim in the wilderness. From the day that you came out of the land of Mitsrayim until you came to this place, you have been rebellious against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
9.8: “Even in Ḥorĕḇ you made 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 wroth, so that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was enraged with you, to destroy you.
9.9: “When I went up into the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the Covenant which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 made with you, then I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I did not eat bread nor did I drink water.
9.10: “Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 gave me the two tablets of stone written with the finger of Elohim, and on them were all the Words which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had spoken to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire in the day of the assembly.
9.11: “And it came to be, at the end of forty days and forty nights, that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 gave me the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the Covenant.
9.12: “Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, ‘Arise, go down quickly from here, for your people whom you brought out of Mitsrayim have acted corruptly. They have quickly turned aside from the Way which I commanded them, they have made themselves a molded image.’
9.13: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to me, saying, ‘I have seen this people, and look, they are a stiff-necked people.
9.14: ‘Leave Me alone, so that I destroy them and blot out their name from under the shamayim, and make of you a nation stronger and greater than they.’
9.15: “So I turned and came down from the mountain, and the mountain burned with fire. And the two tablets of the Covenant were in my two hands.
9.16: “And I looked and saw that you had sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and had made for yourselves a molded calf! You had quickly turned aside from the Way which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded you.
9.17: “And I took the two tablets and threw them out of my two hands and broke them before your eyes,
9.18: and I fell down before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, as at the first, forty days and forty nights. I did not eat bread and I did not drink water, because of all your sins which you committed in doing evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to provoke Him.
9.19: “For I was afraid of the displeasure and rage with which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was wroth with you, to destroy you. But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 listened to me that time once more.
9.20: “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was very enraged with Aharon, to destroy him, so I prayed for Aharon at that time also.
9.21: “And I took your sin, the calf which you had made, and burned it with fire and crushed it and ground it very small, until it was as fine as dust. And I threw its dust into the stream that came down from the mountain.
9.22: “And at Taḇ’ĕrah and at Massah and at Qiḇroth ha’Tta’awah you made 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 wroth.
9.23: “And when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent you from Qaḏĕsh Barnĕa, saying, ‘Go up and possess the land which I have given you,’ then you rebelled against the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and you neither trusted Him nor listened to His voice.
9.24: “You have been rebellious against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 from the day that I knew you.
9.25: “So I fell down before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the forty days and forty nights, for I fell down because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had said He would destroy you.
9.26: “And I prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and said, O Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, do not destroy Your people and Your inheritance whom You have redeemed in Your greatness, whom You have brought out of Mitsrayim with a strong hand.
9.27: ‘Remember Your servants, Aḇraham, Yitsḥaq, and Ya’aqoḇ. Do not look on the stubbornness of this people, or on their wickedness or on their sin,
9.28: lest the land from which You brought us should say, “Because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was not able to bring them to the land which He promised them, and because He hated them, He has brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.”
9.29: ‘And they are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You brought out by Your great power and by Your outstretched arm.’
